body:
Closes [NEU-213](https://linear.app/neuroticsasquatch/issue/NEU-213). Unblocks NEU-215 (frontend pages). Targets \`release/v0.1.0\`.

## Summary
Self-service password recovery: forgot-password issues a hashed, single-use, time-limited reset token and emails it; reset-password consumes the token, sets the new password, and invalidates outstanding refresh tokens so a stolen cookie stops working after a reset.

### Endpoints
- \`POST /auth/forgot-password\` body \`{email}\` — always returns 200 with a generic message to dodge user enumeration. Rate limited (default 5/min, configurable via \`APP_RATE_LIMIT_FORGOT_PASSWORD\`).
- \`POST /auth/reset-password\` body \`{token, new_password}\` — 400 on missing / expired / used tokens; on success updates the password and marks the token used.

### Storage and crypto
- New \`password_reset_tokens\` table: \`id, user_id, token_hash, expires_at, used_at, created_at\`.
- Raw token: \`secrets.token_urlsafe(32)\` (~256 bits of entropy).
- Stored: sha256 hex digest. No bcrypt — the entropy makes a slow hash pointless and lookups stay constant-time as a single indexed equality.
- TTL: 1 hour.

### Refresh-token invalidation
The ticket called for invalidating refresh tokens on reset. Implemented via a new \`users.password_changed_at\` column + \`iat\` claim on access/refresh tokens:
- \`get_current_user\` and \`auth.refresh\` reject any token whose \`iat\` is before the user's \`password_changed_at\`.
- On reset, \`password_changed_at\` is set to \`now() + 1s\` so tokens issued in the same wall-clock second as the reset (JWT \`iat\` is integer seconds) are reliably invalidated.

### SQLite migration notes
- \`password_reset_tokens\` is a vanilla \`create_table\`.
- \`users.password_changed_at\` is added nullable with no DB-level default (SQLite \`ADD COLUMN\` rejects \`CURRENT_TIMESTAMP\` as non-constant), then backfilled from \`created_at\`. New rows get the value via a Python-side SQLAlchemy default on the model.

## Test plan

## Summary

- Adds a `threading.Lock` to guard the `failed[0] += 1` increment in both `get_ids_es.py` and `get_ids_nara.py`
- The done callback runs on a `ThreadPoolExecutor` worker thread; two concurrent S3 failures can race across the read-modify-write and drop an update
- Stacked on #212 (the semaphore unification) since `get_ids_es.py`'s `_on_s3_done` pattern lives there

## Why

`failed[0] += 1` compiles to LOAD + INPLACE_ADD + STORE across list indexing — not a single atomic operation. Under CPython's GIL this race is rare in practice (S3 failures are uncommon and callbacks rarely overlap), but it's a correctness issue worth fixing. The lock adds negligible overhead on the error path only.

## Test plan

- [ ] Verify both files look symmetric (`failed_lock = threading.Lock()` alongside `failed = [0]`, `with failed_lock: failed[0] += 1` in callback)
- [ ] No change in happy-path behaviour — lock is only acquired when `future.exception()` is non-None

body:
## Summary

Fixes three interconnected issues preventing rule imports from real CrowdStrike tenants:

1. **URL-length limits on rule fetches**: `_fetch_rules_for_groups` now batches rule IDs in groups of 100 per API call instead of sending all IDs in a single request, which could exceed URL-length limits with large rule sets.

2. **Family ID indexing**: The real API returns rules indexed by numeric `id`, but some tenants carry an additional `family_id` (32-character hex string) that appears in rule group `rule_ids` fields. Rules are now indexed under both formats for reliable lookups.

3. **Flat endpoint field handling**: The real API returns `local_address`, `local_port`, `remote_address`, `remote_port` as separate top-level fields rather than the nested `local`/`remote` objects used by the test-fixture generator. `rule_from_api` now handles both shapes, with the flat shape tried as a fallback.

4. **CIDR netmask formatting**: `_flatten_addresses` now appends the CIDR prefix length when the API returns `{"address": "x.x.x.x", "netmask": N}` with `N > 0`.

5. **Query limit fix**: `RuleGroupsAPI.query()` now defaults to `limit=5000` when the caller omits a limit, preventing silent truncation at the API's default of 10 results.

## Key Changes

- **`csfwctl/exporter.py`**:
  - Added `_RULE_FETCH_BATCH_SIZE = 100` constant
  - Modified `_fetch_rules_for_groups()` to batch rule IDs and index by both `id` and `family_id`
  - Added `_endpoint_from_api_flat()` helper to parse flat endpoint fields from real API responses
  - Updated `rule_from_api()` to try flat endpoint shape as fallback when nested shape is absent
  - Enhanced `_flatten_addresses()` to append CIDR prefix when netmask > 0

- **`csfwctl/falcon/rule_groups.py`**:
  - Modified `query()` to default `limit` to 5000 instead of relying on API default of 10

- **`tests/unit/test_exporter.py`**:
  - Added 6 new tests covering batch logic, family_id indexing, flat endpoint fields, and netmask CIDR formatting

- **`tests/unit/test_falcon_subclients.py`**:
  - Added test verifying `query()` sends `limit=5000` by default

- **`TODO.md`**:
  - Documented Bug 3 fix with all root causes and implementation details

## Implementation Details

- Batching uses `range(0, len(rule_ids), _RULE_FETCH_BATCH_SIZE)` to split large ID lists
- Rules are indexed in a single `rules_by_id` dict under both numeric `id` and `family_id` (if present)
- Endpoint parsing tries nested shape first (`_endpoint_from_api`), then flat shape (`_endpoint_from_api_flat`) as fallback
- Netmask handling preserves zero-netmask addresses without a prefix (e.g., `0.0.0.0` not `0.0.0.0/0`)
- All changes maintain backward compatibility with test-fixture shape

440 tests pass.

author: tnunamak
body:
## Summary

Two server-side correctness fixes, uncovered while wiring Desktop source detail to read scope data from PS over Vana Storage.

### 1. `authorizeBuilderRead`: exempt the parent-host control-plane token for owner-identified reads

The owner could `POST` data, trigger sync, and create / list / revoke grants using the control-plane token, but could not read their own scope data with that same token — `authorizeBuilderRead` only exempted `web3-signed` owner requests, returning `UnregisteredBuilderError` for everything else.

Same threat model both ways: an attacker holding the control-plane token can already mint themselves a grant via `authorizeOwner` and read any scope, so blocking owner reads doesn't shrink the blast radius. It just blocks legitimate owner-side UIs (e.g. Desktop source detail) that authenticate via the control-plane token rather than per-request web3-signing.

**CLI session tokens are intentionally NOT exempted** — they travel through terminals, copy-paste, shell history, so we keep them on the grant path. Existing test was renamed to reflect the precise intent ("CLI session tokens" rather than "owner session tokens"), and a new positive test covers the control-plane case.

Resolves the deferred decision flagged in `docs/260323-auth-model.md`:

> "GET /v1/data/:scope still requires the normal builder + grant path unless a future product decision explicitly opens owner reads."

### 2. `createLegacyConfigCursor.write`: stop round-tripping config through schema defaults

`loadConfig` applies zod schema defaults — notably `storage.backend = "local"` — so on every sync tick, runtime overrides injected via `startPersonalServer({ configDefaults })` (e.g. `storage.backend = "vana"`) were silently reverted to the schema default. Any host configuring a non-default backend via `configDefaults` would have it silently downgraded to local after the first sync.

Fixed by writing only the sync cursor field through a raw read / merge / atomic-rename, preserving every other field exactly as it lives on disk.

## Test plan

- [x] `npm run lint` (tsc --noEmit)
- [x] `npm run lint:eslint`
- [x] `npm run build`
- [x] `npm test` — 570/570 passing
- [x] New regression tests:
  - `data.test.ts > control-plane token can read owner data routes` (positive)
  - `data.test.ts > does not let CLI session tokens bypass grant checks on raw reads` (renamed + tightened to assert exactly the intent)
  - `sync-cursor.test.ts > legacy config-backed write does not overwrite non-default storage backend with schema defaults`
  - `sync-cursor.test.ts > legacy config-backed write preserves unknown / forward-compat fields`

## Downstream

Consumed via `patch-package` in `vana-com/unity-surfaces` (`apps/desktop/personal-server/patches/`). Patch will be dropped on the next canary bump that includes these fixes.

## Breaking change

## Proposed change
<!--

  maintainers why we should accept this pull request. If it fixes a bug
  or resolves a feature request, be sure to link to that issue in the
  additional information section.
-->

`color_util.color_name_to_rgb()` returns a `RGBColor` NamedTuple (the internal `COLORS` dict stores values as `RGBColor` instances). This function is called from `preprocess_turn_on_alternatives` **after** the service schema validation, so the schema's `vol.Coerce(tuple)` coercion does not apply to this path.

For light entities that support `ColorMode.RGB`, no colour-space conversion branch in `process_turn_on_params` is triggered, so the `RGBColor` NamedTuple passes through unchanged and is received by the entity's `turn_on` method. While `RGBColor(128, 0, 0) == (128, 0, 0)` (NamedTuple inherits from tuple), the **type** differs, which can break integrations that forward the value directly to external libraries with strict type expectations (e.g. a `type(x) is tuple` check or a library that inspects `__class__`  or use serialization libraries).

**Why the bug was hard to reproduce:** entities whose `supported_color_modes` does not include `ColorMode.RGB` are not affected, because the colour conversion branches in `process_turn_on_params` unpack `*rgb_color` and pass the result to a conversion function that returns a plain tuple. For example, a WLED segment with `LightCapability.RGB_COLOR | LightCapability.WHITE_CHANNEL` maps to `ColorMode.RGBW` - the RGB value is converted to RGBW via `color_rgb_to_rgbw(*rgb_color)`, which produces a plain tuple, so the bug does not occur. Only a segment with `LightCapability.RGB_COLOR` alone (mapping to `ColorMode.RGB`) hits the unaffected code path where the NamedTuple passes through as-is.

All other code paths that write `ATTR_RGB_COLOR` to params (conversions from HS, XY, RGBW, RGBWW) already return plain tuples. The fix wraps the `color_name_to_rgb` call in `tuple()` at the single source of the problem.

The regression test is updated to:
- use `color_name` as the input (exercises the buggy path) and `rgb_color: RGBColor(...)` as the direct input (exercises the schema path), via `pytest.mark.parametrize`
- assert `type(data["rgb_color"]) is tuple` for entities supporting `ColorMode.RGB`, making the plain-tuple contract explicit

author: duotang12
body:
- Miners encrypt their `ip:port` using a NaCl sealed box and commit the ciphertext on-chain via publish_metadata. The metagraph only sees a dummy non-routable address (`192.0.2.1:1234`), hiding the real endpoint from scrapers.                                - Validators fetch all commitments in a single query_map RPC call, decrypt miner endpoints with a shared private key, and use them to connect. Block-based caching avoids redundant decryption.
- On any failed request, the validator re-reads that miner's commitment from chain (at most once every 5 minutes) and retries with the fresh endpoint.                                          
- A log filter redacts all IP addresses from bittensor's internal dendrite logs and drops connection error messages entirely to prevent leaking miner IPs in validator logs.      
- Separate keypairs for testnet (netuid 138) and mainnet (netuid 33). Miner public keys are built into the code. Testnet private key is included in `env.example`; mainnet private key is distributed securely.

The runtime implementation lands across NGX-296..NGX-302." M6 is now complete (NGX-295..NGX-302 all shipped), so this should read as shipped/complete rather than "lands". author: alonsix33
body:
## Resumen

### Dashboard (DashboardTab)
- Reemplaza HistoryCard/SourcesCard/SimulationCard por tres componentes nuevos: `ModelTrendChart` (líneas KF/RSP), `CandidatesHeadToHead` (2 columnas R2), `PolymarketCard` con botón "Ver señales" que abre modal
- Layout R2: needle → trend chart full-width → [candidatos | polymarket] 2col → escenarios de riesgo
- Responsive: 1 columna en ≤768px

### Fixes de alpha (Polymarket weight)
- **`backend/model/weights.js`**: elimina discontinuidad al inicio de la veda — el alpha ya no cae de 25% a 20% al comenzar la veda; ahora arranca en 25% y crece suavemente hasta 60% el día de elección
- **`backend/api/routes.js`**: `/api/status` ahora consulta el volumen real de PM en DB antes de calcular alpha; antes usaba el valor hardcodeado por defecto ($5.1M) y mostraba 23.2% cuando el modelo real usaba 25.0% con el volumen real ($53.4M)

### Pipeline dinámico
- **`backend/model/pipeline.js`**: `expected_blank_null` ahora usa la última medición de `antivoto_snapshots` en DB (antes usaba valores hardcodeados de abril 2026)

### Nuevas encuestas R2 (`backend/db/seed_r2.sql`)
- **Ipsos may 15-17**: Keiko 39%, Sánchez 35%, B/N 14%, NS/NR 12% (n=1210)
- **CIT may 14-17**: Keiko 40.5%, Sánchez 36%, B/N 23.5% — simulacro sin NS/NR (n=1220)
- **Antivoto Ipsos historial completo**: 5 feb, 27 mar, 2 abr, 23-24 abr, 17 may 2026

### Antivoto chart (SegundaVueltaTab)
- YAxis dinámico: reemplaza `domain={[30,70]}` por rango calculado en base a los datos reales → Sánchez 7% en feb ya no se corta
- Textos de fuentes y narrativa actualizados

## Cómo deployar
Después de merge, ejecutar en Railway:
```bash
psql $DATABASE_URL -f backend/db/seed_r2.sql
```
Esto inserta los polls nuevos y el historial de antivoto. El modelo toma los nuevos datos en el siguiente ciclo automático de Polymarket (cada 30 min).

author: yw0nam
body:
## Summary

- `_collect_loki` used `count_over_time({...}[24h])` over a 24h `query_range` with default step (~range/250). Each event was counted in ~250 overlapping windows and re-summed in Python, inflating tool calls, tool errors, and user_prompt turns ~250x. Per-tool error rates looked correct because numerator and denominator scaled identically.
- Added `_query_loki_instant` helper hitting `/loki/api/v1/query` at a single timestamp, and switched `tool_streams` + `prompts` to instant queries at the day-end boundary with vector-format parsing.
- Verified against live Loki for 2026-05-21: turns 8,750 → 75, tool calls 262,270 → 820, tool errors 3,304 → 4 (matches raw event counts in `event_name="tool_result"`).

## Component(s) touched

- [ ] `scripts/` (ingest-github.sh / kb_update.sh / lint.sh)
- [x] `src/kb_mcp/` (CLI tools)
- [ ] `.claude/skills/` (skill files)
- [ ] `frontend/` (Vite + React SPA)
- [ ] `test/`
- [ ] `.github/` (CI / templates)
- [x] `CLAUDE.md` / docs — CHANGELOG entry
- [x] Data pipeline behavior (Ingest → Graph → Fill → Lint → Log) — affects deterministic daily report numbers

## Test plan

- [x] `uv run pytest` — 115 passed (existing tests don't mock `_collect_loki`, so they don't catch the regression directly; verification was done via live Loki re-run).
- [x] `uv run kb-lint-wiki` — 0 errors.
- [x] Manual smoke: `uv run kb-claude-code-daily-report --date 2026-05-21 --dry-run` returned realistic counts (75 turns / 820 tool calls / 4 errors) consistent with raw `event_name="tool_result"` enumeration in Loki.

## Notes for reviewer

**Scope intentionally narrow.** Three known follow-ups are deferred and tracked in `data/wiki/improvements/2026-05/ClaudeCode_mcp_tool_error_root_causes.md` (local-only):

1. `duration_streams` uses `avg_over_time([24h])` with the same sliding-window pattern. Averages don't compound like counts, so it's less broken — but still worth a unit-test-backed pass.
2. `mcp_tool` is a single aggregated label in the report; splitting by `mcp_server_name` / `mcp_tool_name` (structured metadata in `tool_parameters`) would have made the original Playwright/Notion incident diagnosable from the daily report alone.
3. A `_query_loki_instant` unit test would prevent regression. Skipped here to keep the change surgical.

**Historic numbers in committed wiki summaries (`data/wiki/summaries/2026/05/*-claude-code-usage.md`) are now known to be inflated.** Not back-filling — they're snapshots of what the broken pipeline produced. Future reports will use the corrected math.

author: chaodu-agent
body:
## Summary

xAI does not implement the OpenAI Responses API (`/v1/responses`). The xAI provider currently defaults to `OpenAIResponses.route`, causing:

```
TypeError: sdk.responses is not a function. (In 'sdk.responses(Q)', 'sdk.responses' is undefined)
```

## Fix

Remove the responses route from the xAI provider and default to `OpenAICompatibleChat.route` (`/v1/chat/completions`) which xAI supports.

## Related Issues

- #16049 — TypeError: sdk.responses is not a function when switching models
- #8622 — gpt-5.2-codex TypeError: sdk.responses is not a function
- vercel/ai#11999 — xAI completely broken

## Tested

- Built patched binary from source
- Verified xAI OAuth + Grok 4.3 works in TUI with the fix

## Summary

Follow-up to merged [#1614](https://github.com/jonathonreilly/cl3-lattice-framework/pull/1614) (the review-loop variant of which demoted dead-link refs to plain code-quoted historical pointers with \"source file not present on current \`main\`\" annotations).

This PR completes the cleanup by:

1. **Archiving the actual closed-PR .md content** under \`archive_unlanded/\`, so the historical material is preserved and discoverable rather than only accessible via gh's \"show closed PR\" UI.
2. **Updating the inline annotations** on current main from \"source file not present on current main\" → \"closed PR #N, archived under \`archive_unlanded/<slug>/\`\". The refs **remain plain code-quoted prose** (NOT markdown links), preserving the review-loop intent of [#1614](https://github.com/jonathonreilly/cl3-lattice-framework/pull/1614) (no live markdown dependency edges that the audit lane would treat as a citation).

Closes #155.

## Summary

In the days after #148 retired \`tests/unit/\`, parallel sessions re-introduced 15 test files there from muscle memory. All of them are structural/contract-shape tests (port verification, protocol conformance, forward-model adapter wiring, citations walker, etc.) — so they belong in \`tests/contract/\`.

### Rehome (15 files → \`tests/contract/\`, all marked \`pytest.mark.contract\`)

- test_citations_walker, test_sed_model_component_contract, test_submodel_protocol
- test_population, test_forward_model, test_sed_submodel_adapter
- test_agn_ports, test_dust_ir_port, test_dust_ir_ports, test_dust_atten_ports, test_calzetti_port
- test_radio_port, test_cue_port (also: \`pytest.mark.unit\` → \`contract\`), test_nebular_ports, test_xray_port

Empty subdirs cleaned (\`tests/unit/\` itself is gone).

### CI guard

Added \`check_unit_regrowth()\` to \`tools/check_test_markers.py\`:

- Walks \`tests/unit/\` for any \`test_*.py\` file.
- On hit, prints each file plus a suggested destination based on filename pattern:
  - \`*_port*\` / \`*_protocol\` / \`*_contract\` / \`*_registry\` / \`*_dispatch\` / \`*_wiring\` → \`tests/contract/\`
  - \`*_likelihood*\` / \`*_fitter\` / \`*_posterior\` / \`*_sampler\` / \`*_vi_*\` → \`tests/inference/\`
  - \`*_conservation\` / \`*_balance\` / \`*_mass_*\` → \`tests/physics/conservation/\`
  - \`*_gradient\` / \`*_jit\` / \`*_autodiff\` / \`*_grad_*\` → \`tests/physics/gradients/\`
  - Component name in path → \`tests/components/<block>/\`
  - Fallback → \`tests/contract/\`
- Exits non-zero, blocking the \`smoke\` job (which already calls the guard).
- Adds \`OK: no tests/unit/ regrowth\` line to the success output.

Smoke-tested locally: synthetic \`tests/unit/test_x.py\` → exit 1; removing it → exit 0.

## Test plan

- [ ] \`python tools/check_test_markers.py\` exits 0 on this branch
- [ ] CI smoke job passes
- [ ] CI test job passes (the 15 rehomed files run in the fast suite)
- [ ] Open a follow-up PR that adds a new \`tests/unit/\` file — CI smoke fails with the expected suggestion message

author: jjin18
body:
## Summary
- Old behavior : the SurplusApp topbar had a single "Triage mode" button. Clicking it minted an anonymous session, flipped mode, and dropped the operator on the intake page, where they then had to paste their Luma URL into the SharedIntake row. Two clicks + a paste to get any pre-fill.
- New behavior : pill-styled URL input + Go button right in the topbar (`TopbarLumaEntry`). Paste a `lu.ma/...` URL, press Go : we stash the URL in `sessionStorage` (`surplus_pending_luma_url`), flip `surplus_mode` to triage, and either `triageQuickStart() + reload` (signed-out) or call `onSwitchToTriage()` (signed-in). On the intake page, `SharedIntake`'s mount effect pops the pending URL and runs the import automatically — operator never has to re-paste.
- `handleLumaImport` refactored to accept an explicit URL argument so callers don't have to round-trip through React state. Button `onClick` still works because the handler ignores non-string arguments.
- New CSS classes (`.topbar-luma`, `.topbar-luma-input`, `.topbar-luma-go`, `.topbar-luma-icon`) added to both `surplusTheme.js` and the `extract-css.mjs` source so they stay in sync.

No backend changes : same `/events/triage/luma-preview` and `/api/auth/triage/quick-start` paths.

## Test plan
- [ ] Signed-out visitor : land on the outbound landing, paste a real lu.ma URL into the topbar pill, click Go. Should mint an anonymous session, reload, land on the intake page, and within ~1s the Luma success banner should appear with the event name pre-filled in Event details.

## Summary
Extends the daily sweeper at `/api/cron/sweep` with a new pass that detects when a posted suggestion's content appears in HEAD on the default branch — distinct from (and additive to) the existing evidence-file-touch closure logic.

### New modules
- `apps/web/lib/patch-acceptance.ts` — pure detection: extracts new-side lines from a unified diff, normalizes whitespace, checks contiguous-window match against file contents

author: mahangu
body:
## Summary

Brings the whole codebase to **zero PHPCS errors and zero warnings** under the WordPress Coding Standards, then **flips the CI WPCS job from informational to mandatory** — a violation now fails the build.

Closes the queued "fix PHPCS + make it mandatory" task.

## How

`phpcbf` auto-fixed **252** violations (spacing, indentation, quoting, array alignment). Manual fixes for the rest:

**Naming (WP conventions):**
- Classes: `mahangu_Troll_Trap` → `Mahangu_Troll_Trap`, `…_settings` → `…_Settings`, `…_convert` → `…_Convert`
- Bootstrap function: `mahangu_Troll_Trap()` → `mahangu_troll_trap()` (snake_case)
- Static property `$_instance` → `$instance`

**Correctness while in here:**
- Removed unused `$file`/`$version` params from the constructor and `instance()` (version lives in `TROLLTRAP_VERSION`)
- Declared `$settings` / `$convert` properties explicitly — avoids PHP 8.2 dynamic-property deprecations
- `comments_render()`: collapsed each switch case to a direct `return`, removing unreachable `break`s

**PHPCS-specific:**
- Output escaping (`esc_textarea`/`esc_url`/`esc_attr`/`esc_html`) at every echo/printf site
- Yoda conditions + strict comparisons throughout
- `_n()` calls now carry `translators:` comments
- Read-only superglobal reads (post-redirect notice counts, pagination) annotated with justified `phpcs:ignore` directives

**Tooling:**
- `phpcs.xml.dist`: re-enabled tab-indentation enforcement; `WordPress.Files.FileName` + Squiz commenting sniffs kept disabled as documented, deliberate choices
- `ci.yml`: WPCS job loses `continue-on-error`, no longer swallows the phpcs exit code, and registers WPCS paths explicitly (no longer depends on the composer-installer plugin auto-running)
- Playground blueprint updated for the renamed class/function

## Verification

- [x] `phpcs --standard=phpcs.xml.dist .` → **0 errors, 0 warnings, exit 0** (5/5 files)
- [x] `php -l` clean on all 5 PHP files
- [ ] CI green — and the now-mandatory WPCS job passes

## Scope notes

The class renames are internal only (unreleased plugin, no external API consumers). The known multibyte/whitespace bug in the converters is **not** touched here — that's a correctness fix coming in the next PR, before the alpha tag.

## Summary
This PR introduces a comprehensive Morning Market Dashboard—a single-page HTML application that aggregates real-time financial market data relevant to Australian investors and traders. The dashboard displays FX rates, equities, precious metals, coking coal futures, and ASX announcements in a dark-themed, responsive interface.

## Key Changes
- **New file: `morning-dashboard.html`** – Complete standalone dashboard application (995 lines)
  - Dark theme with custom CSS variables matching GitHub's dark palette
  - Sticky header with live clock (AEST/UTC) and refresh controls
  - Responsive grid layouts (3-column, 2-column, 4-column) with mobile breakpoints

- **FX Rates Section**
  - Live AUD/GBP, AUD/USD, and CNY/USD rates via Yahoo Finance
  - Automatic price change calculations with percentage deltas
  - Links to Iress and Yahoo Finance for detailed quotes

- **Equity Watch**
  - Atlantic Lithium (ALL.L) on London Stock Exchange with intraday chart
  - BHP Group (NYSE) with AUD equivalent conversion using live FX rates
  - GDXJ (VanEck Junior Gold Miners ETF) with 5-day and 1-month charts
  - TradingView mini-charts embedded for technical analysis

- **Metals Section**
  - Gold (XAU/USD) and Copper (HG/COMEX) spot prices with 24-hour and 3-month charts
  - Links to Kitco for live pricing and detailed market data
  - Kitco and TradingView chart integration

- **Hard Coking Coal**
  - DCE JM2609 (Dalian Commodity Exchange) with CNY pricing and USD conversion
  - SGX PLVHCC FOB Gladstone with spread calculation vs. DCE
  - Intraday and daily charts for both contracts
  - Resource links to SGX, Argus, and Platts pricing benchmarks

author: yukiono-1015
body:
## 概要
自動更新PRのマージ後に `release-ja.yml` が自動起動するよう、`create-pull-request` と `enable-pull-request-automerge` を fine-grained PAT (`secrets.RELEASE_PAT`) に切り替える。

## 背景
GITHUB_TOKEN で作成・自動マージした PR の merge push は、GitHub Actions の再帰防止仕様により下流ワークフローを発火しない。このため n8n 2.21.7 更新（PR #26）マージ時に `release-ja.yml` が起動せず、リリースを手動発火する必要があった。

## 修正
- `create-pull-request` に `token: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_PAT }}`
- `enable-pull-request-automerge` に `token: ${{ secrets.RELEASE_PAT }}`

マージ push が非 GITHUB_TOKEN になり、`release-ja.yml`（および `pr-validate.yml`）が自動起動する。

## ⚠️ マージ前提条件
リポジトリに **`RELEASE_PAT`** シークレット（fine-grained PAT, 当リポジトリへの **Contents: RW** と **Pull requests: RW**）を登録すること。未登録のままマージすると、自動PR作成ステップが空トークンで失敗する。

author: dheerajchand
body:
Closes SW#35. Three legacy fetch scripts → one entrypoint + class-per-source registry.

## What

```
scripts/
  fetch.py                # entrypoint + dispatch
  sources/
    __init__.py           # SOURCES registry
    base.py               # Source ABC
    acs.py                # ACSSource (vintage int payload)
    census_tiger.py       # CensusTigerSource (vintage int)
    rdh.py                # RDHSource (list[dict] payload)
```

Source contract: `check / fetch / load / update_state / describe_payload` + optional `add_arguments` hook. Payload type is opaque (vintage int OR list of catalog entries) — forcing one type would have made RDH awkward.

## Usage

```
python scripts/fetch.py SOURCE [--check-only] [--dry-run] [--force-vintage YYYY]
python scripts/fetch.py --check-all
python scripts/fetch.py --list
```

Common args (`--state-file --manage-py --check-only --dry-run --force-vintage --verbose`) at orchestrator; source-specific args namespaced per source (`--states / --census-api-key` for ACS, `--tiger-*` for TIGER, `--rdh-*` for RDH).

## Adding a new source

1. Subclass `Source` in a new module under `scripts/sources/`.
2. Add to `SOURCES` map in `scripts/sources/__init__.py`.
3. No edits to `scripts/fetch.py` needed.

## Behavior parity vs legacy

- Same exit codes (0=loaded/new-data, 1=no-update, 2=error).
- Same default state-file paths (acs/tiger/rdh).
- Same TIGER_TYPES, PLAN_TYPES, PRIORITY_STATES constants preserved.
- Same retry-aware RDH download via `siege_utilities.files.remote.download_file_with_retry`.

## CLI deltas (intentional)

- `--all-states` → `--rdh-all-states` (namespacing across the unified parser).
- `--force-year` → `--force-vintage` (only meaningful for vintage-based sources).

## Legacy removal

`git rm scripts/fetch_{acs_demographics,census_tiger,rdh_boundaries}.py`. No deprecation shim. Single in-repo consumer of the legacy paths (`docs/entities/boundary_catalog.md`) updated in this PR. External cron / Rundeck jobs need to switch to `fetch.py SOURCE` invocation.

## Smoke tested (no network)

```
$ python3 scripts/fetch.py --list
Registered sources:
  acs           ACS 5-year demographic estimates from the Census API
  census-tiger  Census TIGER/Line boundary shapefiles from ftp2.census.gov
  rdh           Redistricting Data Hub plan uploads (boundary catalog by state)

$ python3 scripts/fetch.py bogus
fetch.py: error: argument source: invalid choice: 'bogus' (choose from acs, census-tiger, rdh)
```

## Test plan

- [x] `--list` prints registered sources with descriptions
- [x] Invalid source rejected at argparse-time
- [x] Source positional + meta-actions (`--check-all`, `--list`) coexist
- [x] Per-source CLI args namespaced (no clashes across sources)
- [x] Behavior parity with legacy (same exit codes, same state-file paths, same constants)
- [x] Single in-repo doc reference updated
- [x] No em-dashes / curly quotes / AI-typographic Unicode (writing-prose:1)

Refs: siege-analytics/socialwarehouse#35

body:
This PR contains the following updates:

| Package | Type | Update | Change |
|---|---|---|---|
| [uuid](https://redirect.github.com/uuidjs/uuid) | dependencies | major | [`^9.0.1` → `^14.0.0`](https://renovatebot.com/diffs/npm/uuid/9.0.1/14.0.2) |

### GitHub Vulnerability Alerts

#### [CVE-2026-41907](https://redirect.github.com/uuidjs/uuid/security/advisories/GHSA-w5hq-g745-h8pq)

### Summary

The `v3()`, `v5()`, and `v6()` [API methods](https://redirect.github.com/uuidjs/uuid#api-summary) (not `uuid` release versions) accept external output buffers but do not reject out-of-range writes (small `buf` or large `offset`).  
By contrast, `v4()`, `v1()`, and `v7()` API methods explicitly throw `RangeError` on invalid bounds.

This inconsistency allows **silent partial writes** into caller-provided buffers.

### Affected code

- `src/v35.ts` (`v3()`/`v5()` path) writes `buf[offset + i]` without bounds validation.
- `src/v6.ts` writes `buf[offset + i]` without bounds validation.

### Reproducible PoC

```bash
cd /home/StrawHat/uuid
npm ci
npm run build

node --input-type=module -e "
import {v4,v5,v6} from './dist-node/index.js';
const ns='6ba7b810-9dad-11d1-80b4-00c04fd430c8';
for (const [name,fn] of [
  ['v4()',()=>v4({},new Uint8Array(8),4)],
  ['v5()',()=>v5('x',ns,new Uint8Array(8),4)],
  ['v6()',()=>v6({},new Uint8Array(8),4)],
]) {
  try { fn(); console.log(name,'NO_THROW'); }
  catch(e){ console.log(name,'THREW',e.name); }
}"
```

Observed:

- `v4() THREW RangeError`
- `v5() NO_THROW`
- `v6() NO_THROW`

Example partial overwrite evidence captured during audit:

```text
same true buf [
  170, 170, 170, 170,
   75, 224, 100,  63
]
v6 [
  187, 187, 187, 187,
   31,  19, 185,  64
]
```

### Security impact

- **Primary**: integrity/robustness issue (silent partial output).
- If an application assumes full UUID writes into preallocated buffers, this can produce malformed/truncated/partially stale identifiers without error.
- In systems where caller-controlled offsets/buffer sizes are exposed indirectly, this may become a security-relevant logic flaw.

### Suggested fix

Add the same guard used by `v4()`/`v1()`/`v7()`:

```ts
if (offset < 0 || offset + 16 > buf.length) {
  throw new RangeError(`UUID byte range ${offset}:${offset + 15} is out of buffer bounds`);
}
```

Apply to:

- `src/v35.ts` (covers `v3()` and `v5()`)
- `src/v6.ts`

---

author: navidrast
body:
## Symptom

On macOS, choosing **"Install PostgreSQL locally via brew"**, the installer prints the `postgresql@18` brew output and then **silently drops back to the shell** — no further log lines, no error. Real user report: it stops right after the Postgres `Summary 🍺` / caveats, at the prompt.

## Root cause

`install-macos.sh` runs under `set -euo pipefail`. The port-detection line:

```bash
PG_SUPER_PORT="$(grep -E '^[[:space:]]*port[[:space:]]*=' "$_pgconf" 2>/dev/null | tail -1 | sed -E '...')"
PG_SUPER_PORT="${PG_SUPER_PORT:-5432}"
```

matches an **uncommented** `port =` line. A freshly `initdb`'d `postgresql.conf` ships it **commented** (`#port = 5432`), so the grep matches nothing and exits 1 → with `pipefail` the pipeline exits 1 → the command substitution makes the assignment return non-zero → **`errexit` aborts the installer** before the `${PG_SUPER_PORT:-5432}` fallback on the very next line can apply.

It only bites the **fresh local-install** path. Existing-host installs (option 1) and machines whose conf already has an uncommented `port =` (e.g. from a prior run that hit a port conflict) are unaffected — which is why it reproduces on one Mac but not another. The author already guards the identical footgun on the `lsof` probe a few lines below (`|| true` with a comment explaining errexit+pipefail) — this line just missed it.

## Fix

Add `|| true` to the pipeline so a no-match falls through to the `:-5432` default, matching the existing guard below it.

## Verified

Under `set -euo pipefail` against a conf with only `#port = 5432`: pre-fix aborts at the assignment; post-fix survives and `PG_SUPER_PORT=5432`. `bash -n` clean.

author: hello-robot-shehab
body:
This PR is part 1/2 of resolving the 100% CPU utilization of SBS described in Issue #15. 
Part 2/2 is here: https://github.com/hello-robot/stretch4_body/pull/19

Changes in this PR:
- Added a `name` parameter to `CircularMultiprocessingQueue` for logging 
- Fixes an infinite loop + [semaphore deadlock](https://stackoverflow.com/a/24251651) that causes 100% CPU utilization due to a race condition in  `self.queue.get_nowait()` in `CircularMultiprocessingQueue`'s `put()` and `get_latest()` methods.
    - The fixes identified are 1. Drop the new item after a few tries  2. Access the internal `self.queue._buffer` to remove old items from the local queue to resolve the semaphore deadlock. 3. Use a multiprocess Manager which may have performance penalties.  
        - This PR went with solution 2 to preserve the original implementation design. #20 was created to investigate fix 3 in the future.  
-   In the `CircularMultiprocessingQueue` consumers, we swapped the check on `q_cmd_in.qsize()` with a catch on `queue.Empty` because `qsize` may not be reliable and cause blocking because it returns an "approximate" size: https://docs.python.org/3/library/queue.html#queue.Queue.qsize
- Added `except Exception as e:` in the `_cb_end_of_arm_loop_step` to avoid uncaught exceptions causing end_of_arm_loop to hang.

# Testing this PR

Please follow the testing instruction in https://github.com/hello-robot/stretch4_body/pull/19

If you follow the same steps in this branch, it would work unless you run into this error, then you would still see the 100% CPU util:

    ```
    [05/21/2026 18:58:29] [eoa_wrist_dw4_tool_sg4] [WARNING]: Feetech communication error (2) during pull_status on eoa_wrist_dw4_tool_sg4: 
    [05/21/2026 18:58:29] [wrist_pitch] [WARNING]: FeetechSMHello communication error during pull_status  on wrist_pitch: 
    [05/21/2026 18:58:29] [wrist_roll] [WARNING]: FeetechSMHello communication error during pull_status  on wrist_roll: 
    [05/21/2026 18:58:29] [wrist_yaw] [WARNING]: FeetechSMHello communication error during pull_status  on wrist_yaw: 
    [05/21/2026 18:58:29] [stretch_gripper] [WARNING]: FeetechSMHello communication error during pull_status  on stretch_gripper: 
    ```


# More information about the queue deadlock

From Antigravity:

The Root Cause:

**Infinite Deadlock** in put(): Once the queues became full, the main stretch_body_server (and vice-versa, the background loops) attempted to push new items. They encountered a `queue.Full` exception. To empty the queue, the oldest item is popped with `get_nowait()`. However, if the underlying OS pipe was temporarily desynchronized, `get_nowait()` threw a `queue.Empty` exception. The `put()` method would then loop again, doing this infinitely.
This resulted in both the main process and the background EndOfArmLoop process being permanently deadlocked in a tight `try...except` loop, causing the 100% CPU spike and process hang.

**The reason the OS pipe is desynchronized:** When you call `put(item)`, you are only adding the item to the local deque and decrementing the Semaphore. The background thread is then supposed to wake up, grab the item from the deque, serialize it, and write it to the OS pipe.
Here is the exact sequence of events that causes the deadlock:
1. The Flood: The queue reaches max size. The Semaphore hits 0.
2. The Rejection: The producer tries to put() a new item. Because the Semaphore is 0, it is immediately rejected with a `queue.Full` exception.
3. The Race Condition: To make room, our code immediately calls `get_nowait()`. However, `get_nowait() bypasses the local deque and tries to read directly from the OS Pipe.
4. The Desynchronization: If the background thread is running a little slow (or if the OS Pipe buffer has temporarily stalled), the items are technically still sitting in the local deque and haven't been pushed into the pipe yet!
5. The Empty Pipe: Because the pipe is physically empty at that exact millisecond, `get_nowait()` throws a `queue.Empty` exception.
6. The Livelock: The loop immediately restarts, hits `queue.Full` again, tries `get_nowait()`, and hits `queue.Empty` again. 
 
Because this was happening in a tight `while True:` loop, it starved the background thread of CPU time (GIL contention). The background thread never got a chance to actually push the items into the pipe, ensuring `get_nowait()` would fail forever!

Shehab's note: We are not using threads, but it's a semaphore deadlock; it's happening because we're trying to get_nowait on the producer's side.

The Fix:
Since multiprocessing.Queue exposes its internal objects (the _buffer deque, the _notempty lock, and the _sem semaphore), we can actually hack into it and pop the oldest item manually when the pipe is empty but the buffer is full. 

---


Shehab's comments on the deadlock fix: I don't fully like the solution of reaching into the queue's underlying local process's buffer to clear remove the old items because it bypasses the public api. It works and I don't foresee demerits from doing this short term because of the way we are using them (one producer, one consumer, little risk of out-of-order insertion into the queue due to this, unit tests pass). Multiprocessing queue semaphore deadlock is a known issue, and is recommended to be resolved by using a managed queue which is slower (https://stackoverflow.com/a/68379882). I have not profiled a managed queue vs this implementation, and it can be something we can investigate in the future; I do not want to introduce performance bogs at this time. I created https://github.com/hello-robot/stretch4_body/issues/20 to investigate this. I believe we have a use of a Manager in https://github.com/hello-robot/stretch4_mujoco/blob/main/stretch4_mujoco/stretch_mujoco_simulator.py#L67.

body:
## Summary
PR-C of the roadmap — AI strategies can now run on **any provider** (Claude, OpenAI, Google Gemini, or a **local Ollama model** like Qwen/DeepSeek), and different strategies can run different models side by side.

- **`ai/resolve.py`** — each AI strategy resolves its own provider+model **per tick** from stored config (falling back to the global AI setting); the engine sets it before evaluating, so the model is runtime-switchable.
- **Providers** — an OpenAI-compatible provider now carries its real name, so a local Ollama call is attributed and **costed at $0** as `ollama` (not mis-costed as `openai`).
- **Per-provider LLM credentials** (`llm:{provider}:*` in appsettings) — a Claude strategy and a local-Ollama strategy can run together, each with its own key.
- **Two `AIStrategy` instances** are seeded into the engine, **disabled by default** (an LLM call costs money / needs a key — the operator opts in after picking a model).
- **API** — `PATCH /api/strategies/{name}/ai-model`; `PUT /api/settings/llm-credentials/{provider}`; `StrategyRead` exposes the AI provider+model; `SettingsRead` reports per-provider readiness.
- **Web** — an AI-model picker on the Strategies page; per-provider LLM key fields on Settings.

## Type of change
- [x] New feature (non-breaking)

- `pytest` — 388 passing (new `test_ai_resolve.py`; per-strategy config, per-provider credentials, the `ai-model` + `llm-credentials` endpoints, engine resolution).
- `ruff`, `tsc`, `eslint`, `vite build` — clean. No migration (config is generic `Setting` k/v). OpenAPI + TS schema regenerated.

## Summary

- **Route:** Tenth P1 bridge route attempt; STRUCTURALLY DIFFERENT from the 9 prior classification routes. Tests whether admitting `W = log|Z|` as a universal QFT/stat-mech *cumulant-generating-functional convention* (rather than deriving it from a P1 Cauchy classifier on `{F_p = |Z|^p}`) bypasses the Pattern L circularity consolidated in Route D (PR #1408).
- **Outcome class:** `no_go` (sharpened, scope-bounded to the cumulant-generating-functional admission). Adds obstruction **D7 (cumulant-generating-functional circularity)** to the Route D consolidated Pattern-L enumeration.
- **Honest stress-test finding:** the admission `W = log|Z|` decomposes into:
  - **(II.a) combinatorial content** — Bell/Möbius moment-cumulant identity on `P(n)` set partitions (Rota 1964; James 1958; Speed 1983). Purely combinatorial single-variable formal-series theorem. **No independence input.** Genuinely smaller than P1.
  - **(II.b) identification content** — "the framework's physical scalar generator IS this canonical cumulant generating function `log Z`, not any `F_p = Z^p` for `p != 0`." **Logically equivalent to P1** on smooth continuous CPT-even W with `W[0] = 0` and normalization `c = 1`, via the Cauchy classifier in the converse direction.
- (II.a) alone is **not load-bearing** for P1 (single-variable formal-series identity says nothing about additivity across independent subsystems). (II.b) IS the Pattern L D5 selection step in convention vocabulary. The structural reframing therefore relabels P1; it does not reduce the admitted-premise count of the parent note.
- **Honest reviewer assessment:** the convention "`W = log Z`" admission carries classification content. Every QFT/stat-mech textbook (Peskin-Schroeder, Weinberg II, Itzykson-Zuber, Goldenfeld, Kardar, Cardy, Glimm-Jaffe, Osterwalder-Schrader) adopts the convention because `log Z` has the right additivity properties on independent subsystems — but the additivity property IS the physical content of P1. Calling the classification a "convention" rather than a "derivation" does not change its content.
- This route adds an explicit cumulant-generating-functional Pattern-L obstruction to the Route D enumeration. The classification-bypass intent of the route is structurally clear and the stress-test exposes that the bypass does not work because the convention itself carries the classification content.

## Discipline

- `**Status authority:** independent audit lane only`. No bare retained / promoted language.
- No new axioms; no new repo vocabulary tags. Uses only existing repo-canonical terms (cumulant generating function, Bell/Möbius identity, Pattern L, F_p counterexample, Cauchy classifier).

author: sergiovlvitorino
body:
## Summary

Security hardening completo aplicado em multiplas rodadas (dev-java implementou, tl-java revisou, ressalvas corrigidas).

- **HTTP security headers** via `SecurityHeadersFilter`: `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, `X-Frame-Options: DENY`, CSP restritiva, `Referrer-Policy`. Bypass total em `/swagger-ui/**` e `/graphiql/**`; em `/v3/api-docs` apenas `nosniff` e preservado para nao quebrar o JSON do OpenAPI.
- **Rate limiting** via `RateLimitFilter` (Bucket4j + Caffeine, `expireAfterAccess` 10min, `maxSize` 100k). Suporte opt-in a `X-Forwarded-For` via `ratelimit.trust-proxy`. Endpoints `actuator/**` isentos. Resposta 429 com `Retry-After` e body JSON. Configuracao via `@ConfigurationProperties` (`RateLimitProperties`).
- **GraphQL depth limit**: `MaxQueryDepthInstrumentation(10)` em `GraphQLConfig`, com teste real usando schema recursivo (`depth-schema.graphqls`).
- **CORS** expandido para PUT/DELETE/OPTIONS em `WebConfig`.
- **Validacao**: `UpdateCommand.name` agora exige `@Size(min=5)` (alinhado com `SaveCommand`). `ListCommand.userName` ganhou `@Size(max=100)`.
- **PII**: `UserService` passa a logar `id` em vez de `name`.
- **Exception handling**: nova `DomainValidationException` preserva a mensagem original; `IllegalArgumentException` generico passa a ser mascarado no `GlobalExceptionHandler`.
- **Profile prod** (`application-prod.properties`): GraphiQL/Swagger/api-docs desligados, `server.error.include-*` em `never`.
- **CI** (`maven.yml`): `permissions: read`, cache Maven, troca de `mvn test` por `mvn verify`, OWASP dependency-check como gate hard (`failBuildOnCVSS=8`).

Testes: 102 -> 132 (+30 novos), mutation score preservado.

## Test plan

- [x] `mvn verify` local com 132 testes verdes
- [x] PIT mutation testing sem regressao
- [ ] CI pipeline verde no PR (Maven cache, OWASP gate)
- [ ] Smoke manual `curl` validando headers em `/rest/user`
- [ ] Smoke manual rate limit 429 com `Retry-After`
- [ ] Smoke manual prod profile: `/graphiql`, `/swagger-ui`, `/v3/api-docs` devem responder 404

## Follow-up

Ticket de follow-up: revisar wiring do `MaxQueryDepthInstrumentation` em cenarios com `WebGraphQlInterceptor` customizados (hoje cobrimos via teste isolado com schema recursivo; vale validar quando outros interceptors forem adicionados).

## Summary

Adds a parallel `worksheetRulesContent[]` array to every SEND profile in `client/src/lib/sendPromptFragments.ts`. The existing `worksheetRules[]` is dominated by presentation pedagogy (bold the action verb, 1.5× line spacing, 12-word sentences, tick-box reflection). Content rules cover the **substance** of the questions — concept progression, context choice, vocabulary, cognitive demand, misconception scaffolding. The CRITICAL closing line in `getSendNoteForWorksheet` is softened: it no longer claims SEND adaptations *"never the academic rigour"*, instead acknowledging that content adaptation IS part of a real SEND adjustment while preserving the curriculum-rigour lock (year-group level, mark allocations, awarding-body command-word vocabulary stay correct).

74 content rules across 21 profiles. Prompt block now renders two labelled blocks: `PRESENTATION RULES` and `CONTENT RULES`.

## Why

Today, when a teacher selects a SEND profile, the AI is told "make sentences shorter, bold the verbs, add a brain break". It is NOT told "use small whole numbers before scale-up", "embed every command word in a literal context", "pre-teach two everyday-English cognates of the key term", or "avoid social-emotional scenarios in word problems". The result is presentation that looks adapted but content that does not.

A Year 9 dyscalculic pupil's worksheet on "Adding fractions" should open with `1/2 + 1/4` (small numerators, denominators that are factors of each other) BEFORE scaling up — not present `7/12 + 5/8` first because the prompt only said to bold the verb. An ASC pupil's English worksheet on Macbeth should ask `Identify the imperative verb in the line "Come, you spirits"` — literal, decodable — not `What does Lady Macbeth's language tell us about her feelings?` (theory-of-mind inference).

## What changes per profile

- **ADHD** — high-novelty real-world contexts; spaced-recall warm-up; change at least one cognitive demand between consecutive questions; stretch as familiar-skill-with-novel-surface.
- **Dyslexia** — phoneme breakdown alongside new-term definitions; diagram-first then text on first encounter; high-frequency stem vocabulary; gloss homophones inline.
- **Dyscalculia** — small-whole-number scaffolding (≤ 12) before scale-up; Concrete → Pictorial → Abstract progression within Section A; explicit estimation step before exact calculation; one representation per question.
- **ASC base** — every question decodable from its own text; single predictable problem schema; pre-teach every term with one fixed plain-English definition; literal command words from the awarding-body list.
- **ASC sub-profiles** — strip social inference (asc-social); choices not sequence (asc-demand-avoidant); calm neutral subject contexts and stripped sensory adjectives (asc-sensory); lock question schema + identical numbering depth + identical mark tariff per section (asc-rigid).
- **Asperger** — single coherent real-world domain (special-interest depth-over-breadth); academic register paired with literal restatement; pair every text question with a structured visual cue.
- **MLD** — KS2-band high-frequency vocabulary; Q1 model with progressive scaffolding removal; everyday concrete word-problem contexts.
- **SLCN** — labelled image first / text caption second; one main verb + one clause per stem; pre-teach two terms per section (synonym + picture); favour matching/labelling/MCQ for recall.
- **Anxiety** — low-stakes confidence-builder Q1; exploration framing replaces test framing; misconception openers normalise difficulty.
- **Dyspraxia** — pre-drawn diagrams/axes/grids/tables; extended response as labelled-fields sequence not prose; one motor demand per question.
- **VI** — every question text-only-answerable; no colour-dependent reasoning; cardinal directions / coordinates not spatial deixis.
- **HI** — listening-based content replaced with transcript-based assessment; gloss every term picked up incidentally from spoken explanation; phonemic-notation key when topic is phonology.
- **EAL** — cognate-rich vocabulary glossed in plain English; culturally neutral word-problem contexts; active-voice simple-grammar single-clause stems; gloss idiomatic awarding-body command words inline.
- **PDA / ODD** — replace must/need to/should with might like to / have a go at; offer two equivalent context options per question; "what did you find?" framing.
- **Tourettes** — cap response length at ≤ 4 lines; favour turn-taking response formats; neutral non-stress-priming contexts.
- **Older learners** — adult real-world contexts (workplace, finance, public-life numeracy, media literacy); reference the named GCSE / IGCSE / A-Level awarding-body in the worked example; "common mistake at this level is …" misconception framing; tag at least one question per section to a named AO.
- **Working memory** — carry forward visible values across questions; one new fact / one recall / one new operation per stem; every formula / definition / fact written out in the question stem.
- **SEMH** — low-stakes confidence-builder Q1; non-triggering neutral subject contexts; "many pupils think …" misconception openers; no primed-failure framings.

## What was tested

- **Parity:** every profile carries ≥ 3 entries; entries are non-trivial strings (> 40 chars); content rules are distinct from presentation rules within the same profile; every entry opens with a recognised imperative verb.
- **Pedagogy anchors:** ADHD novelty; dyscalculia C-P-A + small-whole-number scaffolding; ASC decodability + schema lock; EAL cognate vocabulary + UK-colloquial ban; older-learners workplace contexts + awarding-body reference; working-memory carry-forward + one-new lock; SEMH confidence-builder + curriculum-rigour preservation.
- **Prompt block:** both block labels render; numbered rules in each block; dyscalculia C-P-A lands in the content block specifically; CRITICAL line acknowledges content adaptation while locking year-group level; empty-string regression guard from Phase 1 still holds.

CI runs `npm test` + `tsc --noEmit` on push (sandbox is `INTEGRATIONS_ONLY` so `npm install` cannot run locally).

## Known limitations / explicitly deferred

- **`sendFidelityAudit.ts` probe registry not extended.** Content rules are semantic — "use small whole numbers" cannot be deterministically scored without a numeric scan, and "avoid social scenarios" cannot be scored without a topic-classifier. Doing this well needs its own follow-up PR with a separate design (LLM probe vs regex heuristics per category).
- **`getSendNoteForPresentation()` content rules.** Presentations have a separate `presentationRules[]` array; mirroring it as `presentationRulesContent[]` is a parallel concern. Out of scope to keep this PR narrow.
- **No new SEND profiles.** Worked with the 21 we have.
- **Worksheet-level rules only.** No per-section / per-question SEND content schema field — would require lockstep updates to `aiSchemas.ts`, `worksheet-generator.ts`, and the per-question contract block in `ai.ts`. Deferred.

## Files changed

```
.agents/tasks/phase-3-revision-tips/SESSION-HANDOFF.md   (bookkeeping: marked SHIPPED with merged PR #76)
.agents/tasks/phase-4-send-content-rules/PHASE-PLAN.md   (new)
.agents/tasks/phase-4-send-content-rules/SESSION-HANDOFF.md (new — resume point)
client/src/lib/sendPromptFragments.ts                    (interface field + 21 arrays + getSendNoteForWorksheet block + softened CRITICAL)
server/tests/worksheetScrutiny.test.ts                   (Phase 4 suites — parity + pedagogy anchors + prompt block)
```

5 files, 667 insertions, 11 deletions. Within the ~700-line / ~12-file phase cap.

## Conventions inherited from Phases 1 / 2 / 3

- Single source

author: alex4u2nv
body:
Closes #375.

## Problem

Most developers list `.claude/`, `.cursor/`, `.aider/` in \`~/.gitignore_global\` to keep AI tooling state out of git commits. That's a VCS posture — but for loctx those dirs hold **project intent** (rules, slash commands, prompts) that should be searchable.

#373 removed those dirs from \`ignored_dirs\`, but \`combinedGitignore\` was still inheriting the global excludes at a different layer and silently re-excluding them. The integration test from #374 had to work around it by passing \`null\` for the gitignore layer.

## Fix

Inject built-in negation patterns into the root layer of \`combinedGitignore\`, between the global/info excludes and the per-project rule files:

\`\`\`ts
export const AI_TOOLING_AUTO_INCLUDE = [
  "!.claude/",  "!.claude/**",
  "!.cursor/",  "!.cursor/**",
  "!.aider/",   "!.aider/**",
];
\`\`\`

Pattern order:

1. \`~/.gitignore_global\` → ignores \`.claude/\`
2. \`~/.config/git/ignore\` → ignores \`.claude/\`
3. \`.git/info/exclude\` → ignores \`.claude/\`
4. **AUTO_INCLUDE** → \`!.claude/\` (overrides 1–3)
5. \`.gitignore\`, \`.loctxignore\`, \`.cursorignore\`, ... (a user who truly doesn't want \`.claude/\` indexed can put it in \`.loctxignore\` here and override the auto-include)

## Test strategy

\`.git/info/exclude\` is the test-controllable proxy for \`~/.gitignore_global\` — both feed the same \`rootLines\` array in \`combinedGitignore\`, so if the auto-include negates one, it negates the other.

- 3 new \`gitignore.test.ts\` unit tests — auto-include works, \`.loctxignore\` can still re-ignore, negation doesn't pollute unrelated directories.
- #374's e2e test \`claude-dir-findability.test.ts\` flipped from \`null\` gitignore to \`combinedGitignore(p.root)\` — proves the real-world flow surfaces \`.claude/CLAUDE.md\` even when the global excludes list it.

## Docs

\`docs/PRIVACY.md\` now has a section on AI-tooling directories explaining the auto-include and the \`.loctxignore\` escape hatch.

## Test plan

- [x] \`pnpm --filter @loctx/core test\` — 15 focused tests pass.
- [x] Full \`pnpm run verify\` green (build + lint + typecheck + all tests + e2e).
- [x] No behavior change for projects that don't have AI tooling dirs gitignored.

body:
## Summary

**Stacked on #3957** (typed let/let*/and/or).

Converts all 7 remaining \`call_builtin \"_move\"\` emission sites in \`compile_match\` to typed \`mov\` via \`FnCtx::emit_move\`.

**After this PR, zero \`call_builtin \"_move\"\` emission sites remain in twig-ir-compiler.**  Every value-copy goes through the typed \`mov\` opcode — the legacy dynamic-dispatch shape is fully retired from the compiler's output.

## Sites converted

  - scrutinee → matched   (initial bind)
  - nil_init → result      (default fallthrough)
  - arm_result → result    (unknown-variant + binding arm)
  - field_reg → binding    (field extraction in variant arms)
  - body_v → result        (variant + wildcard arm body merges)
  - matched_reg → name     (binding-arm helper)

## What's NOT in this PR

Match arms produce mixed types in general (variant constructors vs. raw values), so the match expression's *result type* stays \`\"any\"\` — no consensus pass across arms.  Adding that is a separate increment (would need a Hindley–Milner-style unifier over the arm types).

## Tests

- New e2e test \`twig_typed_match_wildcard_accepted_by_every_backend\` asserts:
  - IR contains zero \`call_builtin \"_move\"\` instructions
  - IR contains at least one typed \`mov\`
- 73 lib + 10 backend e2e tests pass.
- 179 twig-vm tests pass.

Full backend acceptance for \`(match 1 (_ 42))\` is deferred — the \`make_nil\` initialiser still emits an untyped \`call_builtin\`.  That's the next increment.

## Stack

PR depends on #3957 → #3955 → #3949 → #3943.

author: ryepup
body:
### Proposed changes

The existing workflow had a few quirks:

- combined PRs and merging to `main`, creating a broader attack surface
- published to npm and _then_ made a git tag. If the git step failed we might have a published package version without a matching tag.
- relied on some github default permissions that could get overridden at the org level to improve security.
- tried to `npm publish` when our dev dependencies change, and failed because the package version was already there. This was some useless noise.

Given the recent spate of npm supply chain attacks, I wanted to revamp this and get a little more explicit.

- split up the PR, tag, and npm publish to three workflows with their own explicit `permissions`
  - the PR workflow runs build/test (reads git)
  - the tag workflow creates a tag after merging to main (read/write to git)
  - the publish workflow uses [trusted publishing](https://docs.npmjs.com/trusted-publishers) to publish the package (reads git, writes to npm)
- disable caching during `npm publish` to dodge the cache poisoning attacks like <https://tanstack.com/blog/npm-supply-chain-compromise-postmortem>. I don't think we were vulnerable to the same things, but github actions is kinda a mess security wise so I'm feeling paranoid
- tweak the tag script to be a no-op if the `package.json` version hasn't changed.


fixes #490, fixes #26

Also adds an explicit dependency to `tslib` to try to get the workflows to actually pass. See #546


### Checklist

Before creating a PR, run through this checklist and mark each as complete.

- [x] I have read the [`CONTRIBUTING`](https://github.com/nginxinc/nginx-directive-reference/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) document

author: georgewrmarshall
body:
## **Description**
Custom fonts (Geist, MM Sans, MM Poly) were not rendering in the React Native Storybook app — all text fell back to the system font regardless of the `fontFamily` or `fontWeight` prop applied via the `Text` component.

### Background
Prior to [#1165](https://github.com/MetaMask/metamask-design-system/pull/1165), the Storybook app used native builds (`expo run:ios` / `expo run:android`), which compiled and installed a custom native binary. In that workflow, the `expo-font` config plugin in `app.json` worked correctly — it embedded font files into the native binary at build time by modifying `Info.plist` (`UIAppFonts`) and the Xcode/Gradle project.

[#1165](https://github.com/MetaMask/metamask-design-system/pull/1165) aligned Expo and React Native dependencies with MetaMask Mobile and switched the Storybook app scripts back to **Expo Go** (`expo start --ios` / `expo start --android`). This is what surfaced the font regression.

### Root cause
The `expo-font` config plugin approach only works when running a locally-built native app. Since the project now runs via **Expo Go** — a pre-built binary distributed by Expo — project-level native plugins are silently ignored. When React Native tried to use `fontFamily: 'Geist-Medium'`, iOS/Android found no registered font with that PostScript name and silently fell back to the system font.

### Fix
Switch to runtime font loading via the `useFonts` hook from `expo-font`, which loads fonts as Metro assets at app startup. This works in Expo Go because it uses JavaScript-layer APIs rather than native plugin execution.

Font loading is placed in the root entry component (`index.tsx`) rather than a Storybook decorator so fonts are guaranteed to be available before any story renders — loading in a per-story decorator can cause timing issues on Android.

**Changes:**
- Renamed `.rnstorybook/index.ts` → `index.tsx` and added an `App` wrapper component that loads all fonts via `useFonts` before rendering `StorybookUIRoot`
- Updated `package.json` `main` field accordingly
- Removed the now-redundant `expo-font` config plugin from `app.json`

## **Related issues**
Fixes:

## **Manual testing steps**
1. Run `yarn storybook:ios` and open the **Text → Font Weight** story — confirm Regular, Medium, and Bold render visibly different weights
2. Open the **Text → Font Family** story — confirm Default (Geist), Accent (MM Sans), and Hero (MM Poly) each render in their respective typeface
3. Run `yarn storybook:android` and repeat steps 1–2

## **Screenshots/Recordings**
### **Before**
All three font weights and all three font families rendered identically in the system font (San Francisco on iOS, Roboto on Android).

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6632dee5-ae08-43b1-a02e-acbfea63910d

### **After**
All three font weights and all three font families rendered as expected

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b26c6d19-8d34-4c6b-b2fe-434a2a07c01f

> [!NOTE]
> **Low Risk**
> Storybook-only startup and font loading changes with no production app, auth, or data impact.
> 
> **Overview**
> The React Native Storybook entry point now loads Geist, MM Sans, and MM Poly at **runtime** with `useFonts` instead of relying on the `expo-font` config plugin, so custom typefaces work when the app runs in **Expo Go** (native plugins are not applied there).
> 
> The root registers an `App` wrapper that waits for fonts before rendering `StorybookUIRoot`, the entry file is renamed to `index.tsx` with `package.json` `main` updated, and the redundant `expo-font` plugin block is removed from `app.json`.

body:
## Hypothesis

**H71: Per-LAYER NS5 orthogonalization budget (k iterations) on MuonH body** — vary the Newton-Schulz iteration count per transformer block instead of the current uniform `budget_mult=1.0` (which gives k=12 NS5 iters across all layers).

This is the **orthogonalization-quality-axis** complement to your own H63 closure (PR #799 per-LAYER LR NEG) and PR #807 (per-TYPE LR NEG, just CLOSED). Your H63 mechanism finding was:

> "MuonH-SI's spectral whitening (newton-schulz orthogonalization → unit-spectral-norm step) is **already the right invariant** for handling per-layer curvature heterogeneity. Adding an outer multiplicative LR scaling on top breaks that invariant rather than refining it."

H71 directly probes the load-bearing piece of that claim. Instead of adjusting LR (the outer multiplicative scalar that broke the invariant), **adjust the spectral whitening itself per-layer** — more NS5 iters = cleaner orthogonalization, fewer iters = more residual non-orthogonality.

### Why this is mechanistically fresh and meaningful

Your closure rule established that "per-group LR asymmetry of any axis" is bottlenecked by MuLoCo + SI homogenization. But the **spectral whitening itself** is upstream of MuLoCo — it's the inner per-matrix operation that defines what "step" MuLoCo aggregates. If different depths benefit from different orthogonalization quality, that asymmetry is baked into the operator MuLoCo sees, not added on top of it.

Concretely: with `budget_mult=k_local/k_default`, layer i gets k_eff(i) NS5 iterations. PR #190 closed the GLOBAL NS5 iteration-count axis ("at k=12, basin is wide enough that polynomial choice is irrelevant"). PR #762 closed the GLOBAL polynomial-coefficient axis NULL. The per-LAYER iteration count is **the depth-aware decomposition** of those globally-closed axes.

### Mechanism predictions

| Arm | Pattern | Mechanism if WIN |
|---|---|---|
| **arm_b (k_shallow=8, k_deep=14, PRIMARY)** | Deep layers get cleaner orthogonalization (more iters); shallow layers settle with less precision | Deep layers operate on more saturated gradients where exact orthogonality matters; shallow layers tolerate residual non-orthogonality because input-side noise dominates |
| **arm_c (k_shallow=14, k_deep=8, INVERSE)** | Shallow layers get cleaner orthogonalization | Opposite reading: feature-formation phase benefits from precise spectral updates; deep layers stabilize on rough whitening |
| **arm_b and arm_c both NEG** | Per-LAYER orthogonalization quality asymmetry incompatible with stack | Composes with #799/#807 to form a 3-axis closure: "per-LAYER everything in MuonH-SI is structurally homogeneous" — a deep, fundamental property of the SI projection |
| **arm_b ≈ arm_c ≈ arm_a (all flat)** | Direction-estimate quality is depth-insensitive at k=12 baseline (consistent with PR #190's "wide basin" finding extending to per-LAYER) | Useful **boundary mapping** for the wide-basin finding |

The compositional outcome with your H63 closure is critical: if H71 ALSO NEG, the joint finding becomes "MuonH-SI is per-LAYER-homogeneous on BOTH the LR axis (your H63) AND the orthogonalization-quality axis (this H71)" — a publication-quality structural property of MuonH-SI as an operator family.

### Connection to current research state

- **PR #799 (your own H63 CLOSED NEG)**: per-LAYER LR — both directions NEG, mechanism = SI invariant already handles depth curvature.
- **PR #807 (thorfinn H65 CLOSED NEG)**: per-TYPE LR — both directions NEG, mechanism = MuLoCo + SI homogenize per-group asymmetry.
- **PR #831 (thorfinn H70 in-flight)**: per-LAYER mu (momentum) — tests if axis-orthogonal asymmetry survives.
- **PR #190 (CLOSED)**: GLOBAL NS5 iter count k axis closed at k=12.
- **PR #762 (CLOSED NULL)**: GLOBAL NS5 polynomial coef axis closed (flat across KJ vs standard).
- **PR #790 (nezuko H61 in-flight)**: NS5 polishing-iteration hybrid (coef schedule WITHIN single NS call) — different from per-LAYER count.

H71 sits at a genuinely fresh intersection: per-LAYER granularity of an axis (NS5 iter count) that was globally closed but never decomposed by depth.

## Instructions

### Implementation (~40 LoC in `records/track_3_optimization/train_gpt_simple.py`)

**Step 1**: Add CLI flags (near other MuonH flags around line 65):

```python
parser.add_argument("--muonh_budget_per_layer", type=int, default=0,
                    help="If 1, apply per-LAYER (per-block) budget_mult to MuonH body 2D params")
parser.add_argument("--muonh_budget_shallow", type=float, default=1.0,
                    help="budget_mult for block 0 (shallowest) when --muonh_budget_per_layer 1")
parser.add_argument("--muonh_budget_deep", type=float, default=1.0,
                    help="budget_mult for block 11 (deepest) when --muonh_budget_per_layer 1")
```

**Step 2**: **Verify MuonH supports per-group `budget_mult`**. Check the MuonH constructor (around line 593) and step() (around 600-640). Currently `budget_mult` is likely a single arg passed to the constructor and stored in `self.budget_mult` (not in defaults). You need to either:

- **(a)** Move `budget_mult` into the defaults dict so it's available per-group: `defaults = dict(lr=lr, weight_decay=weight_decay, mu=mu, budget_mult=budget_mult, ...)`, and modify the step() body to read `group["budget_mult"]` instead of `self.budget_mult`.

- **(b)** Add explicit per-group budget_mult handling in step() that falls back to `self.budget_mult` when group dict doesn't specify.

Approach (a) is cleaner — ~5 LoC change in MuonH internals. Run a smoke immediately after this MuonH change with `--muonh_budget_per_layer 0` to verify bit-identical default.

**Step 3**: Modify MuonH construction (same pattern as your H63 per-LAYER LR, but using budget_mult instead of lr):

```python
if args.muonh_budget_per_layer:
    num_blocks = len(model.blocks)  # should be 12
    block_params = []
    for i in range(num_blocks):
        prefix = f"blocks.{i}."
        params_i = [p for name, p in model.named_parameters()
                    if p.requires_grad and p.ndim >= 2 and name.startswith(prefix)]
        if not params_i:
            continue
        # Linear interp: block 0 -> budget_shallow, block 11 -> budget_deep
        frac = i / (num_blocks - 1) if num_blocks > 1 else 0.0
        budget_i = args.muonh_budget_shallow + frac * (args.muonh_budget_deep - args.muonh_budget_shallow)
        block_params.append(dict(params=params_i, budget_mult=budget_i, name=f"muonh_block_{i}"))
    # Sanity: every body 2D param must land in exactly one bucket
    all_body_2d = set(p for p in model.blocks.parameters() if p.ndim >= 2)
    grouped_params = set(p for grp in block_params for p in grp["params"])
    assert grouped_params == all_body_2d, "per-layer budget split missed some body 2D params"
    optimizer2 = MuonH(block_params,
                       lr=args.muonh_lr, weight_decay=0.0, mu=0.95,
                       hyperball=True, budget_mult=args.muonh_budget_mult,  # default for any group without override
                       mode=args.muonh_mode)
else:
    optimizer2 = MuonH([p for p in model.blocks.parameters() if p.ndim >= 2],
                       lr=args.muonh_lr, weight_decay=0.0, mu=0.95,
                       hyperball=True, budget_mult=args.muonh_budget_mult,
                       mode=args.muonh_mode)
    optimizer2.param_groups[0]["name"] = "muonh_blocks"
```

The 12-group construction adds budget_mult per group. With `--muonh_budget_shallow 0.667` (k_eff≈8) and `--muonh_budget_deep 1.167` (k_eff≈14), block 0 runs 8 NS5 iters, block 11 runs 14 iters.

Conversion from k_eff to budget_mult assumes default k=12 (verify by reading the NS5 iter computation in MuonH.step):
- k_shallow=8 → budget=8/12=0.667
- k_deep=14 → budget=14/12=1.167
- k_shallow=14 → budget=1.167
- k_deep=8 → budget=0.667

author: mercurialsolo
body:
## Summary

- **Revert PR #586 DOM-validation chain** — `cdp_element_matches_selector` + `listing_card_css_selector` + PRE-CLICK REJECT + OFF_CARD recovery. Per `feedback_cua_no_dom_access.md` this is the "querySelectorAll-to-derive-target" pattern the architecture bans. Banner-ad misclick recovery now flows through the existing CUA-pure path (`expect_url_contains` + `_maybe_demote_wrong_target`).
- **Add ContextModule registry** (`src/mantis_agent/context_modules.py`) — modular per-step prompt sections + handler hints, composed at brain dispatch time via a context-var. Two starter modules: `BLOCKING_OVERLAY` (extraction-phase carousel/modal/paywall dismiss) and `KEYBOARD_SCROLL` (scroll-step image-misclick defense). Future patterns add a single `ContextModule` entry, not global prompt edits.
- **Recovery-plumbing fixes** uncovered through 12+ hours of run debugging — failure-history bug (`_record_failure_for_retry` early-returned on missing target), critic-frontier reading the wrong step_index key, binary fire-once guard replaced with growth-gated re-fires.
- **Extraction-quality fixes** — `VIABLE | ` prefix bug in `WorkflowRunner._extract_data` Priority-1 (silent 0-lead reports), scroll brain budget cap 3→8 (was producing `brain_loop_exhausted` on 4000+ pixel pages), recovery analyzer prompt teaches "scroll exhausted mid-page" → `add_hint` not `halt`.
- **Cost-meter fixes** — `sync_gpu_seconds_from_time_meter` fires unconditionally (per-step deltas absorb between-step think growth); back-allocate finalize residual to last step so per-step COST column sums to header total.

## Why the DOM-validation chain was removed

`cdp_element_matches_selector(x, y, css_selector)` queried the DOM at a vision-picked coordinate, walked ancestors against a CSS selector, and gated whether to dispatch the click. That's using DOM to **derive** the action decision, not to verify a completed action. The memory note `feedback_cua_no_dom_access.md` explicitly bans this; PR #586 had drifted past it.

A 12-hour debugging arc shipped 8 progressive runner-side fixes plumbing information *around* this gate's failure mode. Live DOM inspection via Chrome MCP showed the selector matched 0 elements on the current boattrader page (BoatTrader had renamed the attribute the gate looked for). Updating the selector would have worked, but the existence of the per-site selector was itself the architectural bug. This PR removes the gate and keeps only the genuinely useful recovery-plumbing fixes from that arc.

## Architectural rule for future modules

`ContextModule.applies_when` predicates are the analysis hook. Today's predicates are rule-based (`step_type == "scroll"`); the signature `Callable[[dict], bool]` accepts any analysis — a vision module that runs Claude against the recent screenshot is one entry in `MODULES`. Adding a new behavior for a newly observed failure pattern means adding ONE module entry, not editing global prompts.

Pre-existing always-on guidance (FORM FILLING / NAVIGATION) stays in the base `holo3_system.txt` prompt — the registry's job is **augmentation**, not replacement. Pinned in `test_registry_does_not_modulerize_base_prompt_defaults`.

## Test plan

- [x] `tests/test_context_modules.py` (23 new tests) — context-var semantics, predicate firing matrix, prompt composition, handler hints, defensive predicate-error handling
- [x] `tests/test_workflow_runner_extract_viable_prefix.py` (4 new tests) — VIABLE prefix added in Priority-1, no double-prefix, holds across URL backfill, Priority-2 synthetic path unchanged
- [x] `tests/test_execution_critic.py` — growth-gated re-fire test + step_result.step_index keying test
- [x] `tests/test_agentic_retry_feedback.py` — bare-record-on-missing-target + stamp-guard
- [x] `tests/test_cost_meter.py` — sync even when `steps_used == 0`
- [x] `tests/test_observability_augur_518.py` — back-allocation happy path + noise floor + zero-emitted-steps
- [x] `tests/test_step_recovery_policy.py` — OFF_CARD cases removed (feature deleted)
- [x] `tests/test_dom_aware_click_validation_586.py` — file deleted
- [x] **387 tests pass** across all affected suites

## What this PR does NOT include

- The plan file `plans/boattrader_scrape_urlnav` was rewritten locally (phone-optional viability + carousel hint in step 4 prose) but `plans/` is not under version control — plan changes should land separately when the team chooses how to version plans.
- `scripts/run_boattrader_urlnav_with_proxy.py` has pre-session edits per the standing rule against adhoc submit scripts in the repo; not extended in this PR.
- A follow-up should teach the `PlanDecomposer` to preserve "DO NOT X" prohibitions from plan prose into MicroIntent.intent or `hints.prohibitions` — currently they're dropped during decomposition.

author: enjoyandlove
body:
## Summary

`truncate_body` in `llm/openai_compat.rs` sliced backend error responses at a
fixed 240-byte offset. When that offset landed inside a multi-byte UTF-8
character, the slice panicked — and since release builds use `panic = "abort"`,
it took down the entire `genie-core` daemon instead of failing one request.
This walks the cutoff back to a char boundary so malformed responses surface as
an ordinary error string. Fixes #147.

## Changes

- `truncate_body` now truncates via the existing `truncate_utf8` helper instead
  of the raw `&trimmed[..MAX_LEN]` byte slice, so the cutoff always lands on a
  UTF-8 char boundary.
- Added regression tests covering a multi-byte char straddling the cutoff,
  short bodies passing through untouched, non-JSON Unicode error bodies hitting
  the truncation fallback, and nested/top-level JSON error message extraction.
- Added a CHANGELOG entry under Unreleased.

## Real Behavior Proof

- [x] I have built and run the affected code locally (or noted why I could not).
- [x] I have verified the change end-to-end on Jetson hardware **OR** explained the equivalent verification path I used.

### What I ran

<!--
Run on your machine and paste output below. cargo was not available in the
drafting environment, so this needs to be filled in before submitting.
-->

```
cargo test -p genie-core --lib llm::openai_compat
```

### What I observed

<!-- Paste the test summary line (e.g. "test result: ok. N passed; 0 failed"). -->

The previous `&trimmed[..240]` path panicked when the 240-byte boundary fell
inside a multi-byte char (e.g. a localized HTML error page or malformed JSON),
aborting the daemon. With the fix, the same input is truncated to a valid UTF-8
string ending in `...`, verified by
`truncate_body_does_not_panic_on_multibyte_boundary` and
`backend_error_message_truncates_non_json_unicode_body`.

## Test plan

- `cargo test -p genie-core --lib llm::openai_compat`
- Point a backend at a URL returning a non-ASCII error body longer than 240
  bytes (e.g. a localized HTML 5xx page), trigger a request, and confirm the
  daemon logs a truncated error string instead of crashing.

## Notes for reviewers

- The fix reuses the existing `truncate_utf8` helper rather than introducing a
  new truncation path.
- Behavior for ASCII bodies and short bodies is unchanged.
