author: sbp
body:
@alitheg This is a draft, really, but I'd appreciate a review anyway!

This PR sends out warnings if a release has been inactive for 80 days. When it reaches 90 days, it deletes it. It makes an exception on the first go round: it warns everybody about the new policy on their old releases, but then the counter starts from 0. In other words they have 180 days, or however old the release is now (90 days or more) plus another 90 days. This added quite a lot complexity, but I think is worth doing.

There are all sorts of challenging race conditions and so on, and the net result is that releases should be deleted, so we should be careful to ensure that this works, and probably do a rollout only on dev. I'm publishing this to `altera` so that it _doesn't_ automatically deploy to the dev container, which comes from the `sbp` branch. As another safety measure, the actual deletions are protected behind a boolean. In other words, this PR won't actually delete anything anyway, but to do so all we have to do is change one flag.

There are lots of inelegant things about this PR that I dislike. One of the main ones is that I had to duplicate a lot of code to the foundation admin role in the storage interface, because the system caller needs it. Review tools _very strongly_ recommended adding yet another new class in the role hierarchy for system calls. I did add something similar to that just recently, allowing system calls to say "I have this ASF UID and I'm acting on behalf of it, but I don't want you to authenticate anything about that ASF UID as I vouch for it myself". That's fairly easy in comparison, however, because it uses the existing roles in the hierarchy. I've also just added participant release managers as a new role, which is the first new role since the storage interface was created, and am not keen on adding another one already.

author: pressel
body:
## Summary

This PR adds a testing-only SatAdj unit test that verifies conservation through the public MultiFab microphysics flow:

`Init -> Copy_State_to_Micro -> Advance -> Copy_Micro_to_State`

The new test checks that SatAdj conserves the quantities it should conserve for its qv/qc-only saturation-adjustment contract:

- density,
- total non-precipitating water, `rho * (qv + qc)`,
- fixed-pressure latent-energy invariant, `rho * [T + (L/cp) qv]`.

The latent-energy check reconstructs the before and after temperatures using the pre-adjustment pressure, matching the fixed-pressure path used by the SatAdj cell adjustment.

The test also includes explicit coverage checks to ensure the conservation test actually exercises:

- non-zero initial `qc`,
- non-zero final `qc`,
- an all-evaporation case with final `qc` near zero.

SatAdj has no precipitating species, so this test intentionally does not introduce `qp`, rain accumulation, or surface-precipitation checks.

## BFB / testing-only note

This is a testing-only change. It modifies only SatAdj unit-test code and does not change production source, model numerics, physics, runtime behavior, or input options. Therefore, this PR is expected to be BFB for all ERF simulations.

author: asbrings
body:
## Summary

Tested against **iPhone 17 Pro on iOS 26.4.2 + Windows 11 + Python 3.11**.
The project was previously unusable on iOS 17+ (SpringBoard would respring
and the session was torn down before audio could start). This PR makes
the receiver compatible again, adds a working PTPv2 slave, modernizes the
PyAV / NumPy / Windows volume integration, and fixes a couple of
pre-existing playback-stability bugs surfaced during testing.

Closes the same symptom tracked in
[shairport-sync #1942](https://github.com/mikebrady/shairport-sync/issues/1942)
(still open upstream).

## What's included

### iOS 17+/26 compatibility (the blocker fixes)
- `device_info['name']` was `None` because the argparse default never
  persisted — iOS 17+ tears down the session immediately when name is null.
- `do_OPTIONS` `Public` header had a Python implicit-string-concatenation
  bug producing `FLUSHFLUSHBUFFERED` / `PUTSETPEERSXSETMAGICCOOKIE`, and
  was missing `SETPEERS` and `SETRATEANCHORTIME`.
- `timingPeerInfo.Addresses` now enumerates every non-loopback IPv4 + IPv6
  on the host (was one IP); `ID` is now an IP string, matching shairport-sync.
- Default feature bitmask aligned with shairport-sync's known-working value
  (`0x1c340405c4a00`).
- `set_volume_pid` now uses the *data* process PID so pycaw can find the
  PyAudio session — previously volume was silently no-op on Windows.

### PTPv2 slave (sub-ms accuracy on Wi-Fi)
- New `ap2/connections/ptp_messages.py` — IEEE 1588-2008 codec.
- New `ap2/connections/ptp.py` — ordinary-clock slave + PI servo on UDP
  319/320. Handles one-step and two-step Sync.
- New `ap2/connections/ptp_clock.py` — `PTPDisciplinedClock` shared
  across processes via `multiprocessing.Array`.
- `ap2-receiver.py`: SETPEERS / SETPEERSX now spawn/respawn the slave
  with the sender's IP list and ClockID; the shared array is allocated
  once per AP2Server and threaded through Stream into Audio.
- `ptp_selftest.py` — mock-master loopback test that converges
  end-to-end without an AirPlay sender.

The audio scheduler intentionally does **not** consume the disciplined
clock — see the playback-stability section for why.

### Audio pipeline / dep updates
- `requirements.txt`: drop `av==8.1.0` (no longer builds on Python ≥ 3.10
  because `distutils.msvccompiler` was removed). Add `numpy` (required by
  PyAV `to_ndarray()`) and platform-conditional `pycaw` on Windows.
- PyAV 14+ made `AudioCodecContext.channels` read-only — use `layout`.
- `AudioResampler` may return planar frames even when asked for packed —
  use `to_ndarray()` + explicit interleave; `bytes(frame.planes[0])` was
  picking up channel 0 only and producing pitch-shifted crackling.
- PyAudio `frames_per_buffer` raised from `4` to `1024` (the 4-frame
  default underruns WASAPI continuously and produces zipper noise).

### Playback stability
- `AudioRealtime.serve()` resend-storm fix (pre-existing bug): every
  RTCP TIME_ANNOUNCE wake was re-issuing REXMIT_REQUEST for every missing
  seq still in the buffer, flooding the sender's control port and
  producing audible hiccups every ~2 s on Wi-Fi. Added a 250 ms per-seq
  cooldown + GC.
- `_ptp_now_ns()` in the audio path reverts to local monotonic time. PTP
  re-steps on Wi-Fi were leaking into `msec_to_playout` and stalling
  playback. The PTP slave stays running and remains the right primitive
  for future multi-room work — but the audio scheduler shouldn't see
  step jumps. Documented inline.

### Other
- `ptp.py` `spawn()` uses a module-level entry function rather than a
  nested closure so Windows' `multiprocessing` `spawn` start-method can
  pickle it.

## Test plan

- [x] Loopback self-test: `python ptp_selftest.py` — PTP slave reaches
      SYNCED, residual stable < 2 ms after ~5 s.
- [x] End-to-end on Windows 11 + Python 3.11 + iPhone 17 Pro iOS 26.4.2:
      pair → fp-setup → second SETUP with streams → audio playback →
      volume sync all work.
- [x] PTP debug log on real iPhone shows servo residual < 2 ms
      steady-state; no longer affects playback after the decoupling fix.
- [x] Playback stays smooth across the resend-storm bug after the dedupe
      patch; previously had a 2 s glitch cycle on Wi-Fi.
- [ ] **Not tested**: BUFFERED stream (type 103), AAC / Opus, multi-room,
      Linux / macOS, older iOS.

## Notes for the maintainer

- The iOS 17+/26 compat fixes are the highest-impact piece — the project
  has been effectively broken for any modern iPhone for two years.
- The PTP work is self-contained in three new modules + a self-test;
  audio integration is intentionally minimal (one helper + non-blocking
  wait) so it can be reverted/refined independently.
- Several new files needed `git add -f` due to the root `.gitignore`'s
  whitelist pattern — kept as-is to match existing convention rather
  than reworking the ignore policy.
- Happy to split into multiple PRs if you'd prefer reviewing
  iOS-compat / PTP / audio-deps separately.

author: natashasehgal
body:
Summary:

`processSubqueries` in `translateAggregation` processes subquery expressions in aggregate inputs and filters but skips ordering expressions. A query like `array_agg(a ORDER BY a + (SELECT 1))` fails with a `VELOX_CHECK` in `translateExpr` because the `(SELECT 1)` subquery was never wrapped and exported during the subquery processing pass.

Add the missing `processSubqueries` call for `aggregate->ordering()`, matching the existing pattern for inputs and filter. The call shares the same `SubqueryChain` so correlated subqueries across inputs, ordering, and filter share wrap-and-export state.

Reviewed By: mbasmanova

author: bilchreis
body:
## Summary
This PR implements an inactivity detection system for SEC nodes that monitors data update activity and triggers reconnection when no updates are received within a timeout period.

## Key Changes
- **Inactivity timeout mechanism**: Added a 30-second inactivity timeout that monitors whether the node's last update timestamp has changed
- **Ping/pong heartbeat**: When inactivity is detected, the system sends a ping message and waits for a pong response (5-second timeout) to verify the connection is still alive
- **Automatic reconnection**: If the ping times out, the node transitions to disconnected state and triggers a reconnect
- **Update timestamp tracking**: Modified `SECoP_Parser.update()` to record the timestamp of each data update in the NodeTable
- **State machine integration**: Added `last_seen_update_ts` field to track the last known update timestamp and integrated timeout handling into the initialized state

## Implementation Details
- The inactivity check only runs when the node is in the `initialized` state
- The timeout is reset whenever new data updates are received (detected by comparing current vs. last seen timestamps)
- If the ping/pong exchange succeeds or returns an error, the timeout is rescheduled without triggering reconnection
- The mechanism gracefully handles timeout events in non-initialized states by ignoring them
- Minor code cleanup: removed unnecessary comments in TcpConnection and SECoP_Parser

author: turtle261
body:
Make bitwise predictor and consumer support first-class, including bit-to-byte and byte-to-bit adaptability and interoperability. 


This involves several layers:
1. Adding support for native bitwise RateBackends (previously CTW was this, but only conditionally for AIXI)
2. Bitwiseness is no longer decided by the consumer(i.e. MC-AIXI), but by the predictor -- and we provide helpers for efficient byte-to-bit factorization for both MSB and LSB first.
3. bitwise consumption is now first class: Bitwise Arithmetic Coding, and AIXI usage is now correctly handled using the libraries conversion utilities, or native bitwiseness. 
4. Make mixtures with native bitwise models inherit native bitwiseness recursively.
5. Fix confusing naming of `Ctw` -- which was previously AC-CTW in AIXI paths, but FAC-CTW in compression -- it's now just AC-CTW consistently, with `FacCtw` being the unambigous FAC-CTW path. 


This should open up the way to implement [Secondary Symbol Estimation](https://mattmahoney.net/dc/dce.html#Section_433), and some more useful algorithms which wouldn't otherwise be fit for a bytewise prediction library.

author: parifuture
body:
Closes [EL-483](https://linear.app/parifuture/issue/EL-483). Ships the safety guardrail flagged in the EL-468 epic + EL-481 deploy notes: the user's own email is the #1 sender by volume in the live gmail-mirror (5,792 messages since 2005, more than 2x the next sender — see `memory/projects/inbox-zero.md` 2026-05-18), and the Backfill UI had no opt-out, so any rule like "trash newsletters from this sender" applied to outbound mail would silently trash decades of sent history.

## What changes

**Default behavior (`includeSelfSent=false`):** the worker injects the EmailAccount's own email into the sender filter when `evaluateRun` walks the mirror shortlist. The user's outbox is invisible to the LLM, decisions never get written for it, Gmail never gets touched.

**Explicit opt-in (`includeSelfSent=true`):** sets are unfiltered. If the user also pins `senderScope` to their own address, both the API and the worker emit a structured warning log (`backfill.create.includeSelfSent.targetingOwnAddress` / `evaluateRun: includeSelfSent=true with senderScope targeting own address`) — but the request is **not** blocked. There are legitimate use cases (e.g. "label every email I sent to my landlord") and forcing a hard block would be wrong.

**Forensic audit:** the resolved `excludedSenders` list is persisted on the `BackfillRun` row at evaluate time so we have a server-authoritative record of what was kept out of any given run.

## Code surface

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `prisma/schema.prisma` | `BackfillRun.includeSelfSent Boolean @default(false)` + `excludedSenders String[] @default([])` |
| `prisma/migrations/20260522180000_backfill_include_self_sent/migration.sql` | ALTER TABLE adding both columns with safe defaults |
| `utils/backfill/mirror.ts` | `listSenders` accepts `excludeSenders?: string[]`, lowercases + NOT-IN-clauses |
| `utils/backfill/worker.ts` | `evaluateRun` computes `excludeSenders` from `run.includeSelfSent` + `emailAccount.email`, persists `excludedSenders`, logs the targeting-own-address warning |
| `app/api/backfill/route.ts` | `createBackfillBody` accepts `includeSelfSent` (default false), persists it, emits warn log on the targeting-own-address path |
| `assistant/backfill/BackfillRunConfig.tsx` | New 'Include self-sent mail' checkbox (default off, hint reflects state); inline amber warning when user types their own address into senderScope |

## Tests

`apps/web/utils/backfill/` is now **31/31 green** (was 28/28 — added 3):

- `mirror.test.ts`: `excludeSenders` drops listed addresses (case-insensitive); empty array behaves like unfiltered baseline
- `worker.test.ts`: end-to-end — default excludes own email (`totalSenders=1`, `excludedSenders=[<self>]`), opt-in re-includes it (`totalSenders=2`, `excludedSenders=[]`)

`prisma format` + `prisma validate` both green; `tsc --noEmit` clean for the touched files.

## Out of scope (logged for follow-up)

- VIP/family-sender exclusion (EL-468 epic notes call this out — Chotu's wife is sender #2 with 2,662 messages; future ticket wires the existing VIP infrastructure into the same `excludeSenders` filter)
- 'Top 5 senders by volume' inline preview in the config card (stretch goal in EL-483, separate ticket)
- Hard-block path with typed-confirmation modal (the AC mentioned a modal; we chose a non-blocking inline warning instead — explicit opt-in by definition shouldn't double-prompt)

## Migration safety

The migration only adds two columns with safe defaults (`false` / empty array). No data backfill needed. Existing rows of `BackfillRun` (none in production yet — Backfill went live 2026-05-20 and is still pre-first-real-run on Chotu's instance) get the safe default automatically.

author: jedmund
body:
## Summary

Adds the openclaw bot as a native macOS service on `mac-mini` and restructures llama-swap on `max` so an openclaw chat model can coexist with a heavy coding model in VRAM. The two pieces are bundled because the openclaw default model and the llama-swap group sizing have to be designed together: openclaw is the secondary workload that needs to fit alongside whatever opencode is doing.

### Openclaw native macOS role

- New `openclaw` Ansible role installs Openclaw natively on `mac-mini` (Homebrew Node 24, npm-installed `openclaw`, templated `~/.openclaw/openclaw.json`). Native rather than Docker so it can reach iMessage, Spark Desktop's MCP, and the Apple-app MCPs (Notes, Calendar, Reminders, Mail, Messages); none of those work from a Linux container.
- Sandbox mode `off` (mac-mini doesn't hold the same sensitive files the NUC does); model provider points at llama-swap on max over the LAN at `http://192.168.1.100:11434/v1`.
- Discord channel scaffolding for DM-only personal use (no guilds, no voice). Bot creds + Discord IDs vaulted; `openclaw_discord_enabled` toggles the block off cleanly.
- `goplaces` skill's `GOOGLE_PLACES_API_KEY` is now vaulted and emitted to the gateway env.
- `openclaw.json` template is bootstrap-only ownership: the role writes the file on first deploy and then steps back so the gateway's own `openclaw onboard` flow can edit it without ansible clobber.
- `make deploy-openclaw` target for one-command deploys against just the mac-mini.
- Homebrew PATH is pinned for ansible SSH sessions so deploys don't fail on stock-PATH default shells.

### Gateway routing

- `claw.atelier.house` (renamed from `openclaw.atelier.house` mid-flight to drop the model-name prefix) routes through Traefik on `nuc-mini` to `{{ mac_mini_ip }}:18789`, gated by TinyAuth. New `mac_mini_ip` variable next to the existing `mini_server_ip` / `max_server_ip` refs.
- Subdomain added to ddclient list.
- Also bundled: `search.atelier.house` for SearXNG exposed via TinyAuth (unrelated to openclaw but landed adjacently in the gateway dynamic config).

### Llama-swap group restructure for code+chat coexistence

The chat group was previously single-purpose (`swap: true`, one model resident at a time), which made openclaw and opencode mutually exclude each other in VRAM. Three usage modes are now expressed via two new groups alongside `chat`:

| Mode | Active | Group occupancy | VRAM |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1: solo coding | `minimax-m27-q4` or `gpt-oss` | `code-heavy` (exclusive: true, evicts chat + code) | ~185 / ~125 GB live |
| 2: coexistence | `minimax-m27-iq4` + a chat model | `code` + `chat` (both swap: true, exclusive: false) | ~135 GB code + ~36-54 GB chat |
| 3: idle / chat alone | any chat model | `chat` only | ~36-75 GB live |

Concrete model changes:

- New `code` group, holds `minimax-m27-iq4` retuned to `-c 196608 --parallel 3` (3× 64K slots, ~135 GB live).
- New `code-heavy` group (`exclusive: true`), holds `minimax-m27-q4` (current `-c 262144 --parallel 4`, ~185 GB) and `gpt-oss` (~125 GB). Loading either kicks the chat group out.
- `qwen3.6` (dense Q6 MTP, the new openclaw default) retunes to `-c 131072 --parallel 2` (2× 64K slots, ~36 GB) to coexist with iq4 in mode 2.
- `qwen3.6-flash` (openclaw's vision route) retunes to `-c 131072 --parallel 4` (4× 32K slots, ~54 GB) so image-bearing DMs don't OOM when the code slot is loaded.
- `minimax-m27` IQ3_S entry dropped (iq4 covers coexistence, q4 covers solo, IQ3 had no role). The `minimax-m27` / `minimax:m27` aliases now point at iq4.
- `MODELS.md` gets a new Modes section documenting which chat models are coexistence-safe with iq4. Other chat-tier entries (uncensored variants, gemma family, qwen3-coder) keep their larger contexts; loading one while iq4 is resident may OOM, with the expectation that the user unload the code slot first.

### Openclaw default alignment

- `openclaw_local_llm_default_model` switches from `minimax-m27-q4` to `qwen3.6`. q4 now lives in `code-heavy` and would evict openclaw chat on load, so it's no longer the right default.
- `openclaw_local_llm_models` drops the `minimax-m27-q4` entry (not appropriate to call from chat) and updates `qwen3.6-flash` `contextWindow` to `32768` to match its new 4× 32K slot layout.

## What this does not do

- The launchd daemon install (`openclaw onboard --install-daemon`) is interactive and runs once by hand on the mac-mini console; documented in `roles/openclaw/README.md`. macOS permission prompts (Local Network, Automation, Full Disk Access, Notifications) must be approved there too.
- No restart handler yet. The launchd label isn't known until after onboarding; the role surfaces the `launchctl kickstart` incantation as a debug message when config changes.
- The JSON5 config schema is a best-effort read of the docs. After the first onboarding run, diff `~/.openclaw/openclaw.json` against `templates/openclaw.json.j2` and reconcile.

## Manual prereqs before deploy

The `minimax-m27` IQ3_S GGUF files (`MiniMax-M2.7-UD-IQ3_S-*.gguf`, three shards, ~78 GB) are dropped from the catalog. Remove them from `max` after the deploy so they aren't dangling:

```bash
ssh max 'rm /opt/docker/ai/models/MiniMax-M2.7-UD-IQ3_S-*.gguf'
```

iq4 and q4 GGUFs (`UD-IQ4_XS/` and `UD-Q4_K_XL/` subdirectories) are already in place from prior PRs and stay.

## Test plan

### Openclaw
- [ ] `ansible-playbook --syntax-check deploy/openclaw.yml` passes
- [ ] `ansible-playbook deploy/openclaw.yml` against mac-mini installs Node 24, npm-installs openclaw, writes the config file
- [ ] Run `openclaw onboard --install-daemon` interactively on the mac-mini, approve macOS prompts
- [ ] `curl -s http://127.0.0.1:18789/health` on the mac-mini returns 200
- [ ] `ansible-playbook deploy/infra_gateway.yml` redeploys Traefik with the new dynamic config
- [ ] `https://claw.atelier.house` from a remote device lands on the TinyAuth login then the Control UI
- [ ] DM the bot from Discord; response routes through llama-swap to `qwen3.6` and lands back in DMs
- [ ] DM the bot with an image; response routes through `qwen3.6-flash` (visible in llama-swap logs) without OOM

### Llama-swap groups
- [ ] `ansible-playbook deploy/ai.yml` re-renders llama-swap config; `curl -s http://max:11434/v1/models | jq '.data[].id'` no longer lists `minimax-m27` (IQ3_S); does list `minimax-m27-iq4`, `minimax-m27-q4`, `gpt-oss`, `qwen3.6`, `qwen3.6-flash`.
- [ ] Mode 2: load `minimax-m27-iq4`, then `qwen3.6` from a separate request; both stay loaded (`docker exec llama-swap nvidia-smi` shows two llama-server processes).
- [ ] Mode 1: load `minimax-m27-q4`; the chat-group model (if any) gets unloaded.
- [ ] Confirm flash can load alongside iq4 (vision route): with iq4 resident, send an image-bearing request that hits `qwen3.6-flash` and verify both are resident afterward, no OOM in `dmesg` or llama-server logs.
- [ ] `ssh max 'rm /opt/docker/ai/models/MiniMax-M2.7-UD-IQ3_S-*.gguf'` reclaims ~78 GB; deploy still works (no entry references those files).

```
watchtower exited with code 1 (restarting)
```

`containrrr/watchtower` has been effectively unmaintained since 2024 — `:latest` ships an ancient Docker API client (1.25) that recent daemons reject.

## Fix

- Switch image to `nickfedor/watchtower:latest` (actively maintained community fork, drop-in compatible — same `com.centurylinklabs.watchtower.*` label contract).
- Add `DOCKER_API_VERSION=1.44` as a belt-and-braces guard so we don't relive this if the fork ever drifts.
- Inline comment explains the rationale for the next maintainer.

## Verification on host

```bash
docker compose pull watchtower
docker compose up -d watchtower
docker logs -f watchtower    # should reach 'Watching containers' and stay silent
```

## Risks

- Third-party fork dependency. Active repo, but `:latest` could be re-pinned to a specific tag later if we want immutability.
- No impact on `kdust`, `mcp-gateway`, `ews-mcp-builder` — config-only change scoped to the `watchtower` service.

## What

Replaces the native app's bottom tab bar with a floating navigation FAB, plus two related fixes uncovered while building it. Web mobile is unchanged — it keeps `MobileTabBar`.

### Nav FAB (native only)
- A hamburger FAB locked to the bottom-right corner. Tapping it raises the four destinations in a vertical speed-dial stack — each a label pill beside an icon chip, evenly spaced so labels never overlap.

The `Cards / Binders / Lists` switcher scrolled away with the page. It now sticks to the top of the scroll region; on the Cards page the existing sticky search row pins flush beneath it, forming one 2-row sticky toolbar.

author: copilot
body:
POS software commonly sends `DLE EOT n` (`0x10 0x04 n`) status probe commands before printing. Without a response, the client stalls or aborts the print job.

## Changes

- **`start_printer_server`**: Scans each incoming TCP chunk for `DLE EOT n` sequences and immediately replies with `0x12` (paper present, online, no errors). Stripped from the data passed downstream to the parser. A `pending` buffer handles sequences split across chunk boundaries.
- **`parse_escpos`**: Skips any residual `DLE EOT n` bytes (3-byte jump) to prevent stray characters in parsed output.
- **`_PAPER_OK_STATUS = bytes([0x12])`**: Single-byte constant — bit 1 set (per spec), all error/near-end bits clear.

```
Client → 0x10 0x04 0x04   (DLE EOT 4: paper sensor status request)
Server → 0x12              (paper present, not near end, online)
```

Covers all four variants (n=1–4: printer status, offline status, error status, paper sensor status) with the same `0x12` response.

author: benballintyn
body:
## Summary

The `v0.1.1` tag was created but `pypi-publish.yml` never ran — 0.1.1 didn't reach PyPI.

**Cause:** release-please creates the tag with the default `GITHUB_TOKEN`, and GitHub deliberately does not fire workflows from `GITHUB_TOKEN`-created events (recursion prevention). So `pypi-publish.yml`'s `push: tags` trigger could never fire for an automated release.

## Changes

Stop relying on the tag push as the trigger — make `pypi-publish.yml` a **reusable workflow** and call it directly from `release_please.yml`:

- **`pypi-publish.yml`**: triggers are now `workflow_call` + `workflow_dispatch`, both taking a `tag` input. Every job checks out `ref: <tag>` instead of reading `GITHUB_REF`, so it builds exactly the tagged commit no matter how it's invoked.
- **`release_please.yml`**: the `release-please` job now exposes `release_created` / `tag_name` outputs; a new `publish` job calls `pypi-publish.yml` via `uses:`, gated on `release_created == 'true'`, passing the tag.

A `workflow_call` runs *inside the caller's existing run* — no second event, so the `GITHUB_TOKEN` limitation never applies. No PAT needed; OIDC trusted publishing is unchanged.

## Test plan

- [x] Both workflow YAML files parse; triggers and jobs verified
- [ ] After merge: run `gh workflow run pypi-publish.yml -f tag=v0.1.1` to ship the already-tagged 0.1.1 to PyPI
- [ ] Next release-please release auto-publishes via the `publish` job

## Notes for reviewers

- This is pure CI plumbing (`ci:` — no version bump, no package change).
- `workflow_dispatch` doubles as a manual break-glass and as the mechanism to publish the stuck v0.1.1.
- Confirmed the PyPI trusted-publisher config was already updated to `pypi-publish.yml` (you did this).

author: sysread
body:
## SYNOPSIS

Extend the main-chat `VOICE_BLOCK` with a concrete self-check reflex against reflexive agreement.

## PURPOSE

The **baseline voice block** already names "unearned agreement is a failure mode" as the abstract principle. The trouble is that the principle is **easy to hold up front and easy to lose mid-sentence**, once the user has pushed back with confidence: the model starts a paragraph with "you're right about..." or "you're right to push back" and the concession is out the door before the merits have actually been re-examined.

## DESCRIPTION

**Existing shape.** `VOICE_BLOCK` in `src/lib/chat-prompt.ts` carries the anti-sycophancy posture as dispositional sentences - prioritise correctness over comfort, don't soften, don't validate unearned, plain-spoken not robotic. All disposition, no trigger.

**Change.** Three sentences appended to the same block. (1) Name the **opening phrases** that tend to precede sycophantic concessions ("you're right about...", "you're right to push back", "good point") as a surface-level cue the model can catch on. (2) Three **checks** to run before sending the agreement: is the user actually correct on the merits, are you caving to smooth their reaction, did you assume intent the conversation never established and concede to your own assumption. (3) Closer that names the trade: honest disagreement beats unearned agreement.

**Why this fixes PURPOSE.** The block now tells the model *how to notice* it is about to fail the test, not just *what passing looks like*. The leading comment on `VOICE_BLOCK` is updated to explain the addition.

Notes:
- test coverage matches the existing voice-block test style: grep-style assertions on load-bearing beats (trigger phrase, recheck instruction, smoothing/caving check, assumed-intent check) rather than exact phrasing, so future copy tweaks don't churn the suite
- block grew 3 lines; still small enough to ride every turn without bloating context

author: vppillai
body:
## Summary

Third of 7 PRs from the swarm review. Fixes three concrete data-safety bugs in the migration and admin tooling that the Critic + Cursor reviewers both flagged.

## CRITICAL — C6: Migration / admin scripts silently lose data

The scripts in `scripts/migrate-instance.sh`, `scripts/admin.sh`, and `scripts/add-data.sh` had three independent ways to silently drop data and still report success.

### Bug 1 — Single-page scans
`aws dynamodb scan` with no pagination returns at most one 1MB page. The header comment on `migrate-instance.sh` promised idempotency, which was true for items it saw — but the script never iterated past the first page. A table larger than 1MB would silently lose items, with the script printing \"Done. Migrated N items\" anyway.

Fixed by looping on `NextToken` until exhausted. Each page is concatenated into a single JSON array before processing.

### Bug 2 — Subshell counter swallowed failures
The classic bash trap:
```bash
jq -c '.items[]' "$file" | while read -r item; do
    if aws dynamodb put-item ...; then
        ((success++))
    else
        ((failed++))
    fi
done
```
The pipe puts `while` in a subshell. `((failed++))` updates a different variable than the one read after the loop, so the parent shell always sees `failed=0`. The script printed \"Import complete\" regardless of how many `put-item` calls actually errored.

Fixed by switching to process substitution and moving the counter to a tmp file:
```bash
while IFS= read -r item; do
    if aws dynamodb put-item ...; then
        echo $(( $(cat \"$tmpdir/success\") + 1 )) > \"$tmpdir/success\"
    else
        echo $(( $(cat \"$tmpdir/failed\") + 1 )) > \"$tmpdir/failed\"
        ...
    fi
done < <(jq -c '.items[]' \"$file\")
```

### Bug 3 — No sanity check on migrate
`migrate-instance.sh` had no final count comparison. Added: a dest-table scan + count comparison + non-zero exit if any put-item failed. A partial migration is now loud.

## MEDIUM — M2: Backups exclude transient auth state

The CSV/JSON backup exporters in `add-data.sh` and `admin.sh` previously included `SESSION#*` (live session tokens) and `RATELIMIT#*` (current throttling counters). Both are useless in a restore (sessions tied to live TTLs; rate-limits to current IPs) and become liability material if the backup file leaks.

Fixed:
- Backups now filter out `SESSION#*` and `RATELIMIT#*` rows. Metadata reports the skipped count alongside item count.
- The `CONFIG` row (containing `pin_hash`) is preserved so a full restore can still authenticate. To compensate: `umask 077` before opening the file (lands at 0600 perms) plus a clear warning that the file is credential material.

## Test plan

- [ ] `scripts/migrate-instance.sh --from foo --to bar --dry-run` should still work for a small table.
- [ ] After a real run on the actual prod tables: confirm dest count equals expected and exit code is 0.
- [ ] `scripts/admin.sh` → backup option → confirm the resulting JSON file has `0600` perms (`ls -l`).
- [ ] Inspect the backup: `jq '.export_info'` should show `skipped_transient` field and the warning. `jq '.items[] | .PK.S' | grep -E '^(SESSION|RATELIMIT)#'` should be empty.

## Notes

- Scripts retain backward-compatible CLI flags. Existing invocations are unaffected.
- No backend or frontend code changed. No deploy needed for this PR; merging affects only the local admin tooling.

author: vellum-apollo-bot[bot]
body:
The conversation row context menu (right-click + ellipsis dropdown) renders an **Inspect** item when `onInspect` is provided. The topbar variant in `chat-page.tsx` wires it via `useConversationSecondaryActions.handleInspectConversation`, but `chat-layout.tsx` (the sidebar parent) never passed `onInspect` to `AssistantSideMenu` — so Inspect was silently dropped from sidebar context menus.

### Fix

Wire a lightweight `handleInspectConversation` directly in `chat-layout.tsx` that navigates to `routes.inspect?conversationKey=...`. `InspectPage` already resolves the latest assistant message itself when `messageId` is omitted (`ResolveLatestMessage`), so we don't need to drag transcript state into the layout.

Gate on `canUseLlmInspector(authUser)` to match the topbar behavior (staff/@vellum.ai only).

### Repro
1. Sign in as a staff/@vellum.ai user
2. Right-click any conversation in the sidebar (or click the row's ellipsis)
3. Before: Pin / Rename / Archive / Mark as read — no Inspect
4. After: same + Inspect at the bottom (separator above it)

author: mendo9
body:
## Summary

Bug-fix sweep from **smoke session 03** (docs/smoke-tests/2026-05-22-03-bug-fix-sweep.md). Three real bugs surfaced + fixed:

### Fixes

1. **P1 — `/sign-in` "Use a different email" doesn't reset** *(SignInPage.tsx)*  
Typo your email → submit → Clerk sends OTP → click `← Use a different email` → UI stays on the OTP screen forever because `signIn.create()` with the same identifier doesn't transition `signIn.status` back from `needs_first_factor`. Fix: local `forceIdentifierStep` override flag that the back link sets `true` and the next identifier submit clears.

2. **P1 — Athletes hit `/analytics` and render the coach shell over a wall of 403s** *(Analytics.tsx)*  
Route is auth-gated but not role-gated. Athletes who deep-link land on the page; five coach-only queries fire and 403; the page renders "Messages sent: 0 / Response rate: 0%" derived from empty arrays. Fix: read `/api/me`, derive `isCoach`, redirect non-coaches to `/dashboard`, **and** gate every coach-only query (`useGetAnalyticsVelocity`, `useGetAnalyticsPositionConversion`, `useGetAnalyticsStaff`, `useGetPipeline`, `useGetOffers`) on `enabled: isCoach` so the brief window before the redirect doesn't fire 403s.

3. **P3 — Analytics "Response rate 0%" was misleading** *(Analytics.tsx)*  
The velocity endpoint returns `{messages, offers}`; the SPA renamed `offers → replies` in the transform and the KPI computed `replies / sent` — i.e. `offers / messages`, which read 0% because most demo offers are dated past the recent window. Fix: rename end-to-end to **"Offer rate"**, chart legend "Offers", subtitle "Messages sent vs. offers extended". The metric stays useful (outreach efficiency); a real "Response rate" needs the velocity endpoint to add `repliesFromAthletes` per bucket (noted as future work).

### Deferred (documented in session doc, not in this PR)

- **P2** SignIn OTP persists across hard reloads (this PR mitigates only the in-page back link)
- **P2** `/pipeline` and `/scout` for athletes (same shape as fix #2; better solved with a shared `RequireRole` guard than per-page redirects)
- **P3** Settings "Name: Not set" for demo athlete (Clerk first/last null — cosmetic)

## Test plan

- [x] Typecheck — clean
- [x] Lint — 0 errors
- [x] Unit tests — 565 / 565
- [x] Manual coach: `/analytics` renders new "Offer rate" KPI + "Sent / Offers" legend
- [x] Manual athlete: `/analytics` bounces to `/dashboard` with no 403s in console
- [x] Manual: SignIn `← Use a different email` returns to identifier step and accepts a new email

## DO NOT auto-merge

Per ask — user reviews this one.

## Summary

* Adds GitHub Actions CI that runs on every PR to main: type check, lint, format check, unit tests, and build (build waits for all others to pass first)
* Adds Prettier with `.prettierrc` as the formatting standard; adds `eslint-config-prettier` to disable any conflicting ESLint rules
* Adds a Husky pre-commit hook that auto-formats staged files with Prettier and aborts if any file changed, so developers review and re-stage before committing

## First-time setup for developers

No manual steps — `npm install` installs the hook automatically via Husky's `prepare` script.

## Test plan

* [ ] Open a PR with an unformatted file — format check job should fail
* [ ] Open a PR with correctly formatted code and passing tests — all jobs should pass
* [ ] Commit an unformatted file locally — hook should abort and reformat it
